'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19).
  • In a recent development, extensive security measures have already been announced for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants.
  • The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

In a recent development, extensive security measures have already been announced for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, led by Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London.

But what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic.

"The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal," he told DW. "There is no strategy outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises.".

Nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

This has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)?

According to recent reports, after the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, Merz said: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear.".

According to recent reports, but what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President Antonio Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate claims a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under.

"Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations," Meister noted. "Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that.".

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator.

Industry observers note that at the federal government's regular press briefing, he said: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week.

Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he said: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations.".

Government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question.".

Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: Peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

European supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the matter is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

According to the latest DeutschlandTrend survey on the issue, conducted or German public broadcaster ARD in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

Recent findings suggest that A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

#70746. On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (807 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid.
  • Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system.
  • Sources indicate that hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth.

Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway.

Sources indicate that hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010. Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth.

Industry observers note that it was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) debuted the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005.

That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines.

Recent findings suggest that still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005.

Sources indicate that hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that during its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report. Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft.

It has been revealed that "The spacecraft actually bounced off the surface a few times and spent about 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, but apparently the samplers never fired," Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, told Space.com at the time. There was hope that some material managed to make it inside the collector anyway.

"After all the thrashing about ... there is no way to confirm that," Cheng had said. The second landing on Itokawa occured a few days later on Nov. 26, 2005.

In November 2010, five months after Hayabusa's sample-return capsule touched down in Australia, JAXA declared some good news: Hayabusa did collect 1,500 dust grains from asteroid Itokawa, samples that were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite is collector mechanism not firing.

The ultimate success of Hayabusa spurred the creation of another sample-return mission by Japan: Hayabusa2.

According to recent reports, that probe debuted in December 2014 and arrived at asteroid Ryugu (REE-ooh-goo) in 2018. It collected its own samples and returned them to Earth in December 2020. The Hayabusa2 probe is now on an extended mission to the asteroid 2015 BM510, which it will fly by in April 2028. It had planned to land on a strange asteroid 1998 KY26, but suffered engine trouble that made that rendezvous impossible.

#70744. The Smart Ring Goes to Church

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1343 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

The Smart Ring Goes to Church

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1343 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk.
  • In a recent development, the first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps.
  • Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stressed? Heart rate elevated? If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk. So far, so Silicon Valley. But now you can add reading the Bible to that list of self-soothing activities.

In a recent development, the first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps. Two upcoming devices in particular—Glorify’s Ring and Everblessed Technology’s Elah Ring—connect to hugely popular Christian prayer apps with tens of millions of users, and both claim to be the world’s first Christian smart ring.

Both are first, in their own ways. Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US. The $299 Glorify Ring introduced in July, with reservations open and shipping set for January 2027, but 77,000 units of an earlier beta iteration, the Amen Ring made by faith tech company ConfideIn (which merged with Glorify this May), were given away last Christmas. Everblessed manages the Blessed app, and Glorify has an eponymous app.

Another substantial player in prayer apps is Hallow, aimed at Catholics, backed by Vice President JD Vance’s Narya venture capital firm and celebrity ambassadors, with 24 million installs to date. Hallow’s toe-dip into wearables was a 2024 smart rosary with NFC embedded in the crucifix, made with Italian brand Ghirelli; Everblessed tried an earbud, necklace, and bedside device before settling on the ring design.

Head-to-head on design, the Elah and Glorify rings are both made from titanium alloy, with a thorn-inspired twist for Glorify and a minimalist band featuring a cross for the Elah S1, which is also IP68 waterproof to 5 meters.

For now, the Elah Ring is slightly techier: prayer reminders come via the cross, which glows via an LED, and “gentle” vibrations; these can pulse at certain times of day or be triggered by changes in heart rate and stress levels, picked up by a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor. Glorify’s CEO Henry Costa tells WIRED these emotion-based reminders will land on the Glorify Ring in six months; for now, you can set the times of day you want prayer reminders, track heart rate, blood oxygen, stress, and sleep via the optical sensor.

One addition to the Glorify Ring that Costa states he personally uses “a lot” is recording prayers straight into the built-in mic. The ring has a light to signal when it's recording, and the app transcribes them. Everblessed CEO Ricky Xia says that, after consulting with pastors and owners, the feeling was that voice notes on the ring were seen as “suspicious.” It’s available in-app, but most people don’t pray out loud, and too many features drain the battery life. (The Elah Ring runs for up to six days on one charge; Glorify for four to five days.).

According to recent reports, both companies see the smart ring nudges helping wearers prioritize meaningful quiet time, away from screens, while offering in-app Christian practices as an alternative to Eastern meditation. Glorify offers Bible study, courses, and meditations. Blessed has devotional “anchors,” Bible texts and audio, plus guided breathing. Xia notes he’s happy if the Elah vibrates and a user picks up a paper Bible rather than the Blessed app, while Costa says he’s “crying out to use my phone less.”.

Both Glorify (founded in 2020, now merged with ConfideIn and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area) and Blessed (founded in 2023 and based in San Jose) operate in more than 150 countries. Perhaps the biggest difference between the two rings is their relationship to AI.

Xia is all-in, describing the S1 as an “AI-native” product, with a pastor-complementing, not-replacing FaithMate chatbot in the Blessed app, customized based on preferences, congregation, and depth of learning. ChatGPT is like a “good coworker,” he notes, while FaithMate is designed to be “your friend” and an agent that can also handle secular tasks.

Recent findings suggest that “A lot of our owners not only ask questions about the Bible but also ask about themselves, their relationships with their wives, they’re being bullied at school," Xia notes, stressing safeguards around data storage, encryption, and privacy. "Everyone is going to have some AI that they trust, and how they view that is built on their personal stuff, their private vulnerabilities.”.

Recent findings suggest that costa is more circumspect, treading carefully on the consumer-facing side and noting that the Pope has weighed in with a 6,000-word encyclical on AI. A launch interview with CBN News garnered negative comments: “AI is Antichrist Information,” for one.

“The stance I’ve always taken is that our daily devotional is hand-authored by a team of theologians,” Costa says. “It’s prayed over, and that is a stamp of approval.” He criticizes AI slop prayer apps as inauthentic. Still, he says the Glorify team has already tested “many forms” of AI personalization: “Any time, if we do use AI, it must be very clear to the user.”.

Smart ring owners were finding ways to add faith features to mainstream accessories before these rings came to fruition. For 20 years, timer and reminder apps have helped with prayer schedules, but recent examples are more creative. Heidi Campbell, professor of communication in religious studies at Texas A&M, refers to these DIY upgrades to the Oura ring and devices like the Muse headband as “spiritual mind-body hacking.”.

Oura owners on #christiantiktok chat about how they already use the ring’s stress and HR alerts as a prompt to pause and reflect, as per Elah.

Smart ring people flag changes in resting heart rate and sleep quality with scripture following their daily practice. “It’s really helpful for, like, what was inhibiting me from getting to a meditative or contemplative prayer state?” Campbell says. “It takes some of the mystery out of prayer, I think, but that can also be positive. There is a way to do prayer well and not well.” Ring hackers can also dig into health stats during Lent, Ramadan, and Yom Kippur to analyze energy expenditure and how fasting periods affect their bodies.

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered voice recordings and emerging attempts at emotion tracking are part of a fresh phase for smart rings, indicates Ekta Mittal, a senior analyst of connected devices at CCS Insight. These new “purpose-driven” features extend wearable tech into “new parts of consumers’ daily routines,” Mittal says. She suggests that while Glorify and Everblessed will add value for some, the rings are “not directly competing” with established smart ring giants like Oura, Ultrahuman, and Samsung.

It has been revealed that the pandemic sped up the digital transition of many places of worship when congregations could not meet up in person, encouraging experimentation with social media. So it’s early days for Silicon Valley’s impact on organized religion. Researchers at the University of Würzburg in Germany, led by Ilona Nord, are studying the theological implications of using tech, including smart rings, for spiritual practices, investigating which values are baked into secular devices and apps.

According to recent reports, campbell suggests many Christian groups haven’t stopped to consider the unintentional consequences of cultivating spirituality via personal tech. “All of these things are about individualizing the practice, which is good, but the challenges are for religions which are really focused on communal aspects,” she claims. Not everyone has the money or connectivity to access these gadgets, but also, more existentially, “it puts spiritual development over communal development.”.

Xia points to the Blessed app’s communities, including its Healing Room broadcast feature, which lets pastors go live with sermons. It's not in the Elah app yet, but it's on the roadmap. Costa states communal practice is a core pillar, highlighting the “social layer” of public notes made on Christian texts in-app and an upcoming Glorify Ring feature which will allow a user to pair their device with a family member’s ring: “When your loved one is feeling down, you’ll get a buzz to check in with them.”.

Blackburn earn derby draw for Mowbray and extend Burnley’s wait for home win

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health problems.
  • In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break.
  • Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health problems.

In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.

Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season.

Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message “We’re with you, Tony” on the back and the number 900 on the front.

Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.

The stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth sustained a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.

The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.

But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a Mowbray-tribute T-shirt from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.

Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as Hayden Carter backed off.

The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.

Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.

Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are having the ultimate party in U.S.A.

Industry observers note that nearly one year after the Grammy winner and Liily drummer revealed their engagement, the couple tied the knot on Nov. 21 in Palm Springs, Calif., following five years of dating, Miley confirmed on social media.

It has been revealed that alongside sweet black-and-white photos of the newlyweds, shot by photographer Jose Villa, the "Climb" singer wrote on Instagram Nov. 22, "M + M 11.21.26.".

As for who was there to watch something beautiful happen as Miley, 33, and Maxx, 28, exchanged their vows? Well, her father Billy Ray Cyrus and his partner Elizabeth Hurley were among Miley's loved ones in attendance, as well as Elizabeth's son Damien Hurley, per photos obtained by DeuxMoi.

Meanwhile, Miley’s sisters Brandi Cyrus and Noah Cyrus as well as their mom Tish Cyrus and stepdad Dominic Purcell also witnessed the climb to the Last Song star's next chapter.

And the Hannah Montana alum wasn’t having visions of white, but was the embodiment of one as she stunned in a long-sleeved Saint Laurent by Anthony Vaccarello gown that featured a low-cut back while saying "I do." Meanwhile, the groom matched the guests in a black suit, which was also designed by Saint Laurent, according to a press release from the French fashion house.

Miley—who was previously married to Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2020—began dating Maxx in 2021 after they were set up on a blind date through his bandmate's sister's friend, he told Wonderland magazine in July.

As for the proposal, the couple proved that true love hit them like a wrecking ball when Maxx popped the question during a vacation in Japan, getting down on one knee in a beautiful Japanese garden.

“It was a little dead end, this beautiful Japanese forest-y situation,” Maxx told Wonderland. “She was taking videos, and was turned away. That’s when I got on one knee and tapped her on the shoulder.”.

And although the “Toro” singer admitted that he was so nervous he “could feel my heart pounding,” he was able to pull off the surprise, which Miley shared wasn’t a simple feat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paris Saint-Germain’s miserable season went from bad to worse on Sunday as the team suffered a second straight home defeat with a 1-0 loss to Lyon.

Even before the game kicked off, Lionel Messi bore the brunt of the frustrations of some PSG fans who whistled when his name appeared on the significant screen during the announcement of the starting lineup.

Lionel Messi passes 100 international goals with hat-trick against Curaçao.

After Alexadre Lacazette missed a first-half penalty, Bradley Barcola’s goal 10 minutes into the second period was enough to earn Lyon the three points on a night that PSG rarely looked like threatening the visiting goal.

Lens’ 1-0 victory over Rennes and Marseille’s 1-1 draw with Montepellier means both teams are now just six points behind PSG at the top of Ligue 1, and even the domestic title may slip from the team’s grasp.

The reaction of some fans on Sunday must have felt a world away from the adulation and worship Messi received during his recent return to Argentina for friendlies against Panama and Curaçao as the country continued its World Cup celebrations.

Messi’s arrival at the Parc des Princes was supposed to be the missing piece that would help PSG finally win the Champions League, the trophy the club’s Qatari owners crave the most.

So far, the only major trophy the team has won since Messi joined was Ligue 1 last season, a title – it’s fair to say – PSG would likely have won without him.

Messi has 34 goal contributions in all competitions for PSG this season – 18 goals and 17 assists – second only to Mbappé’s 38 and head coach Christophe Galtier refused to lay the blame for the team’s failures at the Argentine’s feet.

According to recent reports, “I found it [the jeering] hard to listen to,” Galtier told reporters, per the Athletic. “There may be expectations for Messi and Mbappe to unlock difficult situations. Messi tries very hard, they didn’t all work out; but around him, the other players also need to do their jobs.”.

“We can’t expect everything from Leo and Kylian,” he added.

Lionel Messi mania grips Argentina as World Cup celebrations continue.

Up next for PSG is a season-defining week as Galtier’s side travels to a Nice team that is unbeaten in 13 matches, before hosting Lens at the Parc des Princes.

PSG has lost two of its three matches since being dumped out of the Champions League by Bayern Munich last month, and only limped past relegation-threatened Brest with a 90th minute Kylian Mbappé winner.

After his team’s victory, Lyon head coach Laurent Blanc said the Champions League or bust mentality has been detrimental to PSG’s performances.

Industry observers note that “Paris’ problem is when the No. 1 objective of the Champions League is no longer accessible, it seems that the season no longer exists – and at all levels,” he told reporters.

Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that PASADENA, Calif.
  • Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune.
  • Industry observers note that "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a massive milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth, something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary.

Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space.

Industry observers note that "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker stated during Thursday's event.

While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the glitch, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon.

"We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd noted. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently.".

Sources indicate that "But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low.".

Recent findings suggest that according to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the natural aging process for spacecraft.

"These spacecraft are old," she remarked. "All of us old people have our aches and pains, and you know, sometimes it takes longer to stretch out your muscles and remember things, and so we are in a realm where we're going to see more anomalies with Voyager just due to the distance and the age.".

"But we feel Voyager 1, although it's not sending us the telemetry data, it's pointed at the Earth. It's sending us a strong carrier signal, and I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back.".

According to recent reports, and, for anyone curious how Voyager 1's slower twin Voyager 2 is faring, Dodd shared that it is doing very well on its own journey through interstellar space. "Voyager 2 is very healthy. It's continuing its mission. It has three scientific instruments on it," she told Space.com.

"Each spacecraft is basically setting a record every day for longevity or distance," Dodd added about the twin probes.

Despite the communications anomaly — and even though most of the team had been up all night to confirm the one-light-day signal from Voyager 1 — the room was alive with excitement. The Voyagers have been flying for nearly 50 years on a mission expected to last just five years, so the team was beyond ready to celebrate.

According to recent reports, amidst the more technical updates about the mission and its current status out in interstellar space, the event included footage of Voyager light-day celebrations from around the world. From children cheering on Voyager to iconic landmarks lighting up gold in honor of the mission's Golden Record, the Voyager love echoed around the world in photos and videos. The footage of this international celebration was enough to move Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, nearly to tears.

"I actually thought I was going to start sobbing," Fox joked to Space.com after the media briefing. "I think just hearing children's voices and people saying 'We love you, Voyager,' 'Go Voyager' — it just was amazing.".

Industry observers note that and Fox and the mission team members weren't the only ones sharing their love for Voyager. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins beamed down her own video message to the Voyager 1 spacecraft from the International Space Station, sharing in the celebration.

Industry observers note that "Dear Voyager 1," Watkins said. "As an orbiting outpost just 250 miles [400 kilometers] above Earth, we often feel distant yet deeply connected to our home planet. The International Space Station has had crew continuously living off of the Earth for 26 years, seen hundreds of visitors from around the world, and enabled thousands of experiments to advance space exploration.

"While you have been traveling into the unknown for nearly half a century, helping pave our path, together, our two journeys tell a single story of exploration," she continued. "One remains close to home, and the other reaches ever outward. Voyager 1, you have been a beacon of light, a symbol of exploration, a seeker of truth, a carrier of hope, a brave explorer, traveling further than any human hand has ever reached. You represent the very best of what humanity has to offer.

"As you reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, the entire crew of Expedition 75 and people across the planet send you our admiration and our wishes for a safe and continued journey as you begin your post-one-light-day era. There are so many amazing milestones and discoveries to come. You have a universe ahead of you, and you carry with you our collective hopes and dreams. When we look up from Earth, we will always think of you as you continue forward into the great unknown. May you continue shining bright for all of us. Go Voyager 1!" Watkins said, ending her message with a weightless backflip from aboard the station.

Sources indicate that in concluding the media briefing, the mission team invited those in the room who, over the past 50 years (or more, with one person sharing their excitement having worked on Voyager before it was even called Voyager) have worked on the mission in one way or another, to stand up to a round of applause. With mission team members today ranging from those in their 20s to their 90s, the people behind this enduring mission span many generations.

Industry observers note that interestingly, Fox actually began her light-day celebrations earlier in the week. She, alongside writer/producer Ann Druyan — who was the wife of the late astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work helped create the mission's Golden Record and who took the now-famous "pale blue dot" Voyager image of Earth to the public — together lit up the Empire State Building gold.

Industry observers note that "I was actually very privileged to flick the switch and turn on the Empire State Building lights on Tuesday evening [Nov. 17]," Fox, wearing golden Voyager-inspired nail polish crafted by her daughter, told Space.com. "That was just spectacular … I was there with Ann … we were both so giddy with the excitement of doing it … It was amazing. And then going up and standing underneath and seeing the tower was just really, really special.".

While the room lit up with excitement for Voyager's light-day milestone on Thursday, the team was also brimming with anticipation for what lies ahead. As Voyager hurtles toward another major milestone, turning 50 in 2027, it remains an active science mission, and the team remains hard at work to push the boundaries of exploration with these aging probes.

"Voyager right now — the two Voyagers — they're in an area of space that we've never been into. So every single bit of data that comes back is precious because it's unique," Fox said.

In a recent development, "Now we're in a region where the sun's influence is a lot different, and we're in this region where we can start to understand: What is it like out past our sun? What is it like in the space between the stars?" Voyager deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin told Space.com. "We're at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we've seen, living with this star [our sun] to what is out there.".

Industry observers note that "What's next? Voyager is just going to keep on going. You know, people sometimes think, 'When's the mission going to end?' It's never going to end," Fox added to Space.com. "Even when we can no longer talk to Voyager, they're both going to keep going … So there's no end for the Voyager mission.".

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (854 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Snapchat has 3 upcoming ways to help creators get discovered

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A creator's video can put a restaurant on someone's weekend list, send shoppers looking for a product, or make a brand want to work with the person who posted it.
  • 18, Snap announced three updates that make it easier for 1) followers to find places their favorite creators recommend, 2) brands to find creators to work with, and 3) agencies to run those campaigns.
  • Here's how each revision works and how Snapchat's approach compares with what other social platforms are already doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A creator's video can put a restaurant on someone's weekend list, send shoppers looking for a product, or make a brand want to work with the person who posted it. Snapchat wants to integrate more of that routine into Snapchat.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 18, Snap announced three updates that make it easier for 1) followers to find places their favorite creators recommend, 2) brands to find creators to work with, and 3) agencies to run those campaigns. If you're a creator, that could mean more ways to make money from the videos you already post and another place for people to find your recommendations.

Here's how each revision works and how Snapchat's approach compares with what other social platforms are already doing.

Snap Map already works a little like a neighborhood guide. For example, if you tap on a bakery, there's a listing with its hours, directions, and reviews. Now, with a feature called Visited By, Snapchat can also show that a creator you follow has been there and give you a link to their post.

Here's how it works. Using the same bakery example — if a food creator reviews a bakery and tags it in a public post on Spotlight, Snapchat's short-video feed, or posts the review directly to Snap Map with the same tag. Snapchat can then highlight the store on the map for that creator's followers. So if you missed the video when it first went up, you could still come across it while looking for pastry, watch a creator's review, and send the spot to a friend in Chat. The feature is available globally, and Snap says more than 450 million people use Snap Map each month.

Snap claims people already share creators' recommendations in Chat when they're talking about "where to go next or what to buy." Visited By gives them a upcoming way to share a business. Snap also sees the sharing part as a way for creators to reach people who don't already follow them.

"For creators, it means more visibility for the places and experiences they share, helping them connect with their existing followers and build fresh ones as their recommendations are shared with friends," the tech giant wrote.

This announcement comes a few weeks after TikTok gave its own users an in-app way to go from watching a restaurant video to booking a table. In October, it launched Must Eat, a dining guide built from videos, reviews, and comments across the app.

Sources indicate that snapchat is also changing how advertisers find creators to work with. The revamped Snap Creator Network, now in open beta, lets a brand describe the audience it wants to reach, the type of content it needs, or what it hopes the campaign will accomplish. Snap uses AI to suggest creators, and brands can then review how their content performs, save a shortlist, message creators about a partnership, or pay to promote a post they've already made.

"Our aim is to make creator discovery and outreach more efficient, while maintaining the creator's voice within their own communities," Snap wrote in the blog post. "For creators, this means greater opportunities to work with some of their favorite brands and be discovered for the right audience fit, not just follower count.".

Eligible creators can opt in by turning on Brand Partnerships in their Public Profile settings. That lets approved brands reach out directly on Snapchat to work together or to use a video the creator has already posted in an ad.

According to recent reports, sometimes the team reaching out to a creator is an agency working on the brand's behalf. Snap is giving those teams more help, too, through its expanded Creator Agency Partner Program. The program, according to Snap, equips "agencies with the training, support, and incentive access they need to build and scale Creator Ads on Snapchat.".

Recent findings suggest that other social platforms have similar pipelines in place: TikTok One matches advertisers with creators based on a campaign brief, lets brands promote approved posts as Spark Ads, and gives agencies tools to manage contracts and track campaigns. Meta's Creator Marketing Hub, on the other hand, brings creator search, outreach, and Partnership Ads together across Instagram and Facebook.

There's a reason Snap, TikTok, and Meta are all making it easier for brands to find creators and turn their posts into ads. The Interactive Advertising Bureau projected that U.S. creator ad spending would reach $44 billion in 2026, and brands in its research stated finding the right creator was their biggest challenge. The easier a platform makes it to find someone, reach out, and run an ad, the better its shot at a slice of that (pretty large) pie.

Fifa to confirm UK as host for 2035 Women's World Cup

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fifa is set to confirm on Monday that a first football World Cup will be hosted in the United Kingdom since 1966.
  • England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup.
  • A delegation will be present at Fifa's Zurich headquarters with national associations holding a specially arranged virtual meeting, and voting to ratify the co-hosts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup.

Fifa is set to confirm on Monday that a first football World Cup will be hosted in the United Kingdom since 1966.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup.

A delegation will be present at Fifa's Zurich headquarters with national associations holding a specially arranged virtual meeting, and voting to ratify the co-hosts.

The tournament would involve 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

Nineteen venues are proposed by the 'All Together' bid, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Recent findings suggest that fifa's evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five. However, its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed that "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

This is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

Fifa's bid evaluation stated: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues.".

Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium is one of 19 stadiums included in the 2035 bid.

England hosted the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland are also joint hosts of the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, stated: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.".

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed newly introduced Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it will still be considered in its current form.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues.

Recent findings suggest that noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "Wales has been a football nation for 150 years and we have never hosted anything on this scale. World Cup football played here, in front of Welsh children, would change what this game looks like in Wales: in the clubs, in the schools, and in the number of girls who grow up seeing a pathway into it.".

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government noted in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

In a recent development, the Irish Football Association's chief executive Patrick Nelson noted the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country. Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that.".

Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow are the Scottish venues proposed, with Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell saying hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

Recent findings suggest that he added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.".

The special meeting of Fifa's Congress is also set to approve the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Tech Report: Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A display reminds those attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, of their goal: limiting global warming to 1.5 ºC.Credit: Metin Aktas/Anadolu/Getty.
  • Among countries at the COP31 climate summit under way in Antalya, Turkey, there’s a growing recognition that meeting climate targets will require the world to go ‘net negative’, which means removal of more carbon dioxide from the air than is added.
  • According to recent reports, scientists say that climate ‘overshoot’ — exceeding 1.5 °C of warming, a target set in 2015 in the landmark Paris agreement — is now inevitable in the next few years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A display reminds those attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, of their goal: limiting global warming to 1.5 ºC.Credit: Metin Aktas/Anadolu/Getty.

Net zero is no longer enough. Among countries at the COP31 climate summit under way in Antalya, Turkey, there’s a growing recognition that meeting climate targets will require the world to go ‘net negative’, which means removal of more carbon dioxide from the air than is added.

According to recent reports, scientists say that climate ‘overshoot’ — exceeding 1.5 °C of warming, a target set in 2015 in the landmark Paris agreement — is now inevitable in the next few years. Reaching net-zero status would halt the rise in temperatures. But only achieving net-negative status can bring temperatures back below the 1.5 °C threshold this century.

Sources indicate that can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions.

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions.

According to recent reports, that reality has made net negative and the enormous amount of CO2 removal that would be needed to achieve it a prominent idea at the summit. A coalition of eight countries called the Group of Negative Emitters (GONE) has been working to convince other nations to adopt net-negative targets and get serious about CO2 removal. The group revealed that it will be co-chaired by Denmark and Ethiopia, which is hosting next year’s climate summit and could put net negative at the top of the agenda.

“We are in an era of overshoot, and we have to do a lot in terms of removing carbon dioxide,” Ethiopian ambassador Samuel Addis Alemayehu said at a GONE event on 18 November, touting the nation’s progress on reforestation.

In a recent development, some climate campaigners worry that CO2 removal technologies won’t work and that focusing on them could distract countries from cutting emissions. Despite those concerns, the latest draft of the main statement from COP31 recognizes that CO2 removal has a role in addressing the overshoot, and welcomes efforts to “urgently and rapidly” scale up development of removal methods.

According to a United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) report1 released ahead of the meeting, the world can expect about 1.8 °C of warming this century, even in the most optimistic emissions scenario.

Every fraction of a degree above 1.5 °C raises the risk of climate disasters such as wildfires and powerful hurricanes. “COP31 will be judged a failure if we don’t address the overshoot,” said Ilana Seid, Palau’s ambassador to the UN and chair of the Association of Small Island States, at a press briefing held during the summit.

Many countries at the meeting have discussed slashing emissions to limit the size and duration of the coming overshoot. Turkey has pushed to implement a target of 35% of global energy demand being met with electricity by 2035, a proposal that has gained support from more than 75 countries at the conference and is also included in the draft statement.

Sources indicate that but the UNEP report estimates that to recover from overshoot, at least 330 billion tonnes of CO2 would have to be pulled out of the atmosphere this century after the world reaches net zero. Removing that much CO2 would require a vast expansion of existing efforts. Today, about two billion tonnes of CO2 per year are removed by nature-based projects such as reforestation, which takes advantage of the carbon absorbed by growing trees. Scaling up carbon removal swiftly enough to achieve net negative and storing carbon in a more durable form will require technological CO2 removal solutions as well.

Sure, Miley Cyrus can buy her own flowers, write her name in the sand.

But it's hard to argue that anyone can love the three-time Grammy winner better than her newly minted husband Maxx Morando can.

It has been revealed that just under a year after they got engaged, the pair officially said "I do" Nov. 21, according to Entertainment Tonight.

And before the Hannah Montana alum and Liily drummer walked down the aisle, they made sure their guests had the best of both worlds. The couple kicked off the weekend with a rehearsal dinner that was certainly a party in the U.S.A. serving up filet mignon and Maine lobster ravioli.

Sources indicate that and let's not forget the dessert spread, featuring chocolate caramel layer cake, vanilla crème brûlée and raspberry sorbet. Each treat even came with an “M+M” design in honor of the newlyweds.

While the menu was sweet, Cyrus' feelings for Morando are even sweeter.

"We've been together six years, and I've never gotten the ick," she told Zane Lowe in an interview shared by Apple Music Sept. 17. "All of a sudden I got in my head, I was like, ‘Oh my God, we’re about to get married. What if I get the ick?'".

"I asked him, 'What happens if you get the ick once you’re married?'" she continued. "He’s like, 'You deal with it and you move on and you don’t be a baby. The ick is for when you’re in fifth grade.'".

"I think that’s the thing that maybe generations prior didn’t teach us," Cyrus said, "that marriage doesn’t need to be a prison. It can actually be a playground.".

Having watched her union with Liam Hemsworth metaphorically burn after their Malibu home went up in flames in 2018, Cyrus was good with being alone. She was gold, actually.

But when a friend floated the idea of setting her up with 28-year-old Morando on a blind date, she reflected to British Vogue in 2023, "I thought, 'The worst that can happen is I leave.'".

Instead, she found the kinda dream that can't be sold.

Mostly because, this time around, she was looking for more than just a piercing stare and effortless curls.

In the past, she acknowledged in a joint sit down with Tish Cyrus and sisters Brandi Cyrus and Noah Cyrus, her mother had encouraged her to stay "with the wrong guy," she explained to Newly introduced York magazine's The Cut, "'cause they're hot.'".

Though, make no mistake, she insisted of Morando, "My man's hot as hell too. But my man also respects me.".

With the rocker, she continued, "I ended up with a person who means a lot to me and treats me really well and respects me.".

And that's just a few of the far more than seven things she likes about her spouse.

With his birthday mere days before hers, "he’s a Scorpio and so is his grandfather," Cyrus raved during a June 2025 appearance on the Sorry We're Cyrus podcast, "that’s what makes Maxx just so cool because he can sting.".

The "Can't Be Tamed" musician admittedly can get a bit crazy, so she "couldn't be with" someone that doesn't have that edge, she noted. "They would have been toast already.".

But not long after she and Morando turned up at Gucci's Love Parade fashion show together in November 2021, it became clear they had the right recipe.

In a recent development, "We just don't take life too seriously," she told Harper's Bazaar in 2024, describing her frequent collaborator as "very similar" to herself. Decades into her career, she continued, she had a pattern of working "with the people that I love. And Maxx just inspires me so much.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that rockstar Games went above and beyond licensing dozens of existing bangers across almost any genre you can imagine for GTA 6's in-game radio stations, and that's before you even get to the fantastic original score from Justice.
  • Thankfully, Rockstar Games took a cue from how people listen to music in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most important aspects of any Grand Theft Auto game is the soundtrack, and for the first time in the series, GTA 6 doesn't require players to be in a car or near a radio to listen to it.

It has been revealed that rockstar Games went above and beyond licensing dozens of existing bangers across almost any genre you can imagine for GTA 6's in-game radio stations, and that's before you even get to the fantastic original score from Justice. However, one small limitation of previous games in the series was that you couldn't really enjoy all of that music while walking around.

Thankfully, Rockstar Games took a cue from how people listen to music in 2026. Here is how to listen to music in GTA 6 without driving a car.

Recent findings suggest that in real life, most people have a pair of headphones or earbuds handy so they can listen to music on their phones. GTA 6 joins some other open-world action games like Watch Dogs 2 in allowing players to use virtual headphones to jam out to some tunes from a smart device while simply walking around the world. The best part is that you can do this from a very early point in the game, though it will require a little bit of in-game money.

Recent findings suggest that protagonist Jason Duval is perhaps the only guy in Leonida who doesn't own headphones of any kind at the start of GTA 6, so you'll have to go buy some. This can be done at any electronics store in Vice City and the surrounding areas, and you'll know a store sells headphones if the store's icon on the in-game map is a pair of headphones. Convenient!

Unless you really branch out right away and decide to explore the whole map before getting on with the story, the easiest way to get headphones at the start is to drive up north from Jason's neighborhood to the town of Hamlet. Some of the early main story missions will take you there, anyway. What you're looking for is a store called Zeke's Electronics on the north side of Hamlet.

Sources indicate that simply go in and you'll be able to buy either over-ear headphones or earbuds next to the cash register. Over-ear cans will run you about $200, while earbuds cost $119. I can't tell if there's a meaningful difference between the two aside from looks, so just go with whatever you like more.

Once you have your headphones, simply hold left on the D-pad to listen to the radio while outside of a car. I recommend the Dirty South Classics station, personally, but your mileage may vary. SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule returns to Earth from the ISS

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.

The robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov. 20) at 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), while the duo were flying 260 miles (418 kilometers) above western China.

In a recent development, the freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at 5:03 p.m. EST (2155 GMT).

Sources indicate that the Dragon launched Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it was the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program.

The capsule arrived at the ISS on Oct. 15, delivering more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, scientific gear and other supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. It brought a lot of stuff down to Earth, too.

"Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth," NASA officials wrote in an revision on Tuesday (Nov. 17).

"The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth," they added.

According to recent reports, dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. The others — Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, Russia's Progress vehicle and Japan's HTV-X — are all expendable and burn up in Earth's atmosphere to wrap up their first and only spaceflight.

Recent findings suggest that editor's note: This story was updated at 12:20 p.m. ET on Nov. 20 with news of successful undocking, then again at 8:55 p.m. ET on Nov. 21 with news of splashdown.

The even more minimal Z-Trek sandals are also on sale for $45 ($15 off).

These Fjällräven Vidda Pro trousers are my favorite hiking pants thanks the thigh zips that deliver excellent ventilation. The Vidda Pros uses Fjällräven's G-1000 fabric, a 65 percent recycled polyester and 35 percent cotton blend, with pockets everywhere, and nice reinforced knees (with openings for pads). There's even a hatchet loop on the leg.

In a recent development, six Moon Design's Lunar Solo is one of the best single-wall ultralight solo tents you can buy. It's not without its quirks (read the pitching tips), but if you want something more than a tarp, that still weighs just 26 ounces (740 grams), this one is hard to beat. Use the Code YULEHIKE to get the 25 percent off.

Sources indicate that nemo's Hornet tents are some of the lightest freestanding tents around. The 1-person model is my go-to for situations where I might have to pitch on rock or concrete slabs (like staying in towns on a longer bike-packing trip). It's roomy enough for you and all your gear, light enough at 2.25 pounds (without stakes), and packs down remarkably small. It's also held up well in storms, though you will want some extra guy-outs if the wind is really howling (I like Zpacks 1.2-mm dyneema cord for lightweight guy lines).

Sources indicate that this is the bike-packing version of Massive Agnes' popular Copper Spur tent, one of the best backpacking tents around. The only difference, aside from color, is that the pole segments on this model are shorter (to make it easier to store on a bike). The Copper Spur line is very nearly the lightest freestanding tent around (it's just slightly heavier than the Hornet above), and if you happen to use it with trekking poles, you get what I think is the best feature, the covered awning modification for the vestibule. While this is the best deal, the 2-person model is also on sale for 20 percent off.

This is one of my favorite ultralight sleeping bags. There are lighter quilts out there, but when you need the warmth of a mummy bag on those colder nights, this is what I use. It also has the smallest pack size of any bag I've tested in this temperature range. With the included compression sack, this thing is truly tiny. The down fill is PFC-free, 850+ hydrophobic down. The zippers are on the small side, but they slide well and rarely (if ever) snag on the bag. I've slept in this bag down to 20 degrees and never been the least bit cold.

In a recent development, closed-cell foam pads like the Therm-a-Rest Z-Lite Sol are a must-have. They weigh next to nothing (10 ounces for the small), fold up small enough to lash to the outside of any pack, and double as a chair, extra padding on cold nights, table, you name it. I am too old and too soft to be the sort of ultra-minimalist who gets by with just a Z-Lite, but I still have one around on almost every trip I take.

Industry observers note that nemo's Tensor-insulated sleeping pads have the best R-value-to-weight ratio of anything I've tested. The Tensor All-Season featured here sports an R-value of 5.4 and weighs 18.2 ounces. That alone is impressive, but what I love about the Tensor is that it's thick, comfortable, and most importantly, nearly silent. The lighter Trail model is also on sale at REI. Its R-value is only 2.8, though.

Industry observers note that I love my MegaMat, it is hands down the best sleeping experience I've had car camping (I have the auto version that fits in the back of your car). While it's not our absolute favorite mega sleeping pad (that's the slightly lighter, smaller MondoKing), I like the MegaMat better it has slightly better insulation. This deal is on the duo model, which is 72 inches long and 41 inches wide. The single wide MegaMat is also on sale for $195 ($75 off).

According to recent reports, I don't usually bring a chair backpacking—I just sit on the ground. But for some reason, I do love a chair when I'm bike packing, which is where I've used this Nemo the most. It's quite pricey, but it's very light and packs down to a tiny package. The genius part of this chair is that the cover is also a mat that keeps it from sinking into soft ground.

In a recent development, the thing to keep in mind when you shop REI-brand gear is the firm's basic proposition: You get 90 percent of the designer item for 70 percent of the price. It's a strategy that works quite well and has generated some really great, affordable gear. This chair is a good example of that. It's not as nice as the Nemo above—it does wobble a bit, side to side, when you move—but it's still comfortable and half the price.

Sources indicate that this camp chair is the coziest way to hang out around the fire. It is a bit big, heavy, and awkward to fold up and carry, but so long as you have room for it in your vehicle, there's no better way to relax under the stars with your loved ones.

I sincerely hope you never have any need for one of these Sea to Summit bug head nets, but if you do, boy do you. I once did not have one and tried to go backpacking in Michigan’s UP in early May. I lasted about two hours. When I got home, I bought one of these and … still haven't ventured back to that marshy bog of a hike. But I could, and possibly even retain some of my sanity thanks to this thing.

What I said about the chair above goes for this day pack as well; it's an excellent value, especially on sale. I was surprised by how comfortable this thing is, especially because, to look at it, the straps are very lightweight and there's almost no padding. It still managed to carry loads up to 10 pounds without straining my shoulders, and the side stash pockets are fabulously large—major enough for a Nalgene bottle or rain jacket. The Flash 22 is made of 70-denier recycled ripstop nylon, which is on the lighter side, but mine has held up well, even coming through some rough canyon hikes in Utah without any more than mud stains.

It has been revealed that these two pots are my go-to cooking vessels for larger group meals. I find they're just about perfect for boiling up enough water to rehydrate four servings. I don't take the bowls and silverware into the backcountry, but they're handy for camping.

According to recent reports, sure, phones have some of the features you'll get with a satellite messenger, but we still think you're better off with a dedicated device. Garmin's newly introduced inReach Mini 3 Plus now offers some of those phone features—like voice messaging—along with the emergency features and excellent service worldwide. It's also still tiny, well-built, and it has great battery life. A non-Plus model, which doesn't have a speaker and mic, is also on sale.

Sources indicate that the Stash is our favorite all-in-one backcountry cook system. The heat diffuser design is what speeds up boil times (Jetboil claims 2.5 minutes, which I was only able to match indoors in still air), but the real appeal here to me is the way this kit all packs down into itself. For weekend trips, this is the simplest system I've tested when it comes to cooking for two.

Jetboil's larger all-in-one cooking system, the Flash, offers a larger-capacity 1-liter pot that combines an integrated pot and burner into an easy-to-use system. I prefer the more compact Stash above, but if you're cooking for two and are all-in on dehydrated meals, this stove is popular for good reason.

Sources indicate that these dry bags from Sea to Summit have double-stitched, tape-sealed seams that have held up well over the years. I also really like the external lash loops that make it easy to strap to anything with a tie-down anchor.

I like these dry bags for organizing things in my pack. They're not dry bags in the sense that you can submerge them and your gear will be fine, but the 30D silnylon with PCF-free DWR easily sheds a little rain. And they make finding your stuff easy. I put all my cooking gear in a red bag (red for fire), all my water-filtering stuff in a blue bag for, wait for it, water—and so on. I find the 3- and 5-liter bags the most useful, but you can get all the way up to 35L.

According to recent reports, I've noticed that, when trying to lighten their load with a smaller, lighter-weight backpack, people then struggle to fit all their gear. The answer for sleeping bags and clothing is this compression stuff sack, which takes my favorite sleeping bag (the Sea to Summit Spark above) and smashes it down to about half the size of the included stuff sack. You can do the same thing to clothing, especially puffer jackets, but also fleece and merino to some extent, to free up more room in your pack.

Sources indicate that REI’s Big Haul duffel is a durable, water-resistant, gear-swallowing bag for carrying, well, just about everything. It's one of our favorite ways to schlep your gear when flying. It hits the right balance of robust build materials and pockets without being too heavy to lug around all day. The strap system is cleverly customizable, and you can convert it to a backpack.

Once upon a time, in a galaxy far, far away, I traveled around Southeast Asia with an early version of this Osprey pack, living out of it for almost a year. It stood up well to the abuse of overland travel—more than once, I watched a bus driver tie it to the roof of a bus by cinching it down with a rope, pulling with all his weight right down the middle of my pack, like a cheese cutter. The Farpoint survived, and my gear inside did as well, thanks in part to the thickly padded sides, which provide considerable extra cushioning.

Bruce Willis’ wife, Emma Heming Willis, has celebrated their elder daughter’s birthday with a trip down memory lane.

Mabel Willis turned 11 on Sunday, and her proud mom marked the occasion by sharing a montage of family photos and videos taken over the years, set to the song “Pictures Of You” by The Cure.

“Happy 11th Birthday Mabel Ray!” Heming Willis wrote in the caption.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about finding community as a caregiver: 'This journey can feel very dark'.

“Your energy is infectious,” she continued, praising her little girl for the way she “can light a whole room with your smile and warmth.”.

“How you love and care for your family and friends is beautiful to witness. Keep shining my love and always remember to #liveitup,” Heming Willis added.

According to recent reports, heming Willis and Willis married in 2009. Along with Mabel, the couple also have an 8-year-old daughter, Evelyn. Willis also has daughters Rumer, Scout and Tallulah with his ex-wife, Demi Moore.

Willis is clearly a doting dad. One picture in Heming Willis’ montage reveals the “Die Hard” star holding baby Mabel while planting a kiss on her forehead, while a more recent image shows a beaming Willis hanging out in nature with his preteen.

Bruce Willis sings with his family in birthday tribute video from ex Demi Moore.

Recent findings suggest that heming Willis penned an equally heartfelt tribute last month when her husband celebrated his 68th birthday. Sharing a video montage on Instagram, she referred to the actor as “pure love.”.

In February, Willis’ family declared that his speaking disorder, aphasia, had progressed into a form of dementia called frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

It has been revealed that “Today there are no treatments for the disease, a reality that we hope can change in the years ahead,” they remarked in an update shared online. “As Bruce’s condition advances, we hope that any media attention can be focused on shining a light on this disease that needs far more awareness and research.”.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, FTD refers to “a group of disorders caused by progressive nerve cell loss in the brain’s frontal lobes (the areas behind your forehead) or its temporal lobes.” These areas of the brain are generally associated with personality, behavior and language.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.

According to recent reports, make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.

According to recent reports, A blisteringly cold November afternoon in Hull, against a promoted side where the expectation for a team challenging for the title is to win, and perhaps win with minimum fuss, too. On another afternoon, Brighton may have done just that, were it not for the heroics of Hull’s goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis.

But the best teams, the ones that end the seasons lifting the silverware, almost always seem to find a way. Tzolakis was the Seagulls’ scourge with a string of sensational saves that kept Hull in a contest where, for large periods, they were struggling to keep their heads above water.

However, the goal Brighton deserved never arrived – and as this game wore on you wondered if a team like Hull, whose commitment can never be questioned and who are tough to beat on their own turf, could dig in for long enough to provide a sucker punch on the counter. That moment arrived, not perhaps with Oli McBurnie’s goal that broke the deadlock in stoppage time, but two minutes before.

When João Costinha was shown a second yellow card in the 89th minute for a foul on Sorba Thomas, the MKM Stadium responded. They sensed that Tzolakis’s heroics could perhaps produce more than just a point, with Brighton forced to sit in and try to hold out for the closing moments. Hull surged forward, with McBurnie bundling home from close to range to spark delirium among the home support.

It has been revealed that two minutes later, with Brighton now left pressing just to try to find an equaliser, Hull caught them cold and McBurnie would tap into an empty net to seal the most unlikely of victories for the Tigers, who remain unbeaten at home since promotion. This was their first win since August, however, and a welcome tonic to put breathing space between themselves and the bottom three.

“We played against an excellent team who play intensive football,” Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, said. “I wish this feeling would never stop because we’ve had to wait for this.” But this was an afternoon that was as much about Brighton as it was Hull.

In a recent development, A win here would have closed the gap to Arsenal at the top to three points. In the end, this was a huge missed opportunity, with Hürzeler understandably crestfallen post-match.

“In the Premier League you can never expect to win,” he stated. “For us, it’s very key with our identity and every game you have to lift your standards. If you drop, the Premier League is too good and it will punish you.”.

According to recent reports, mcBurnie may have been the hero but there was no doubting the star man was Tzolakis. He denied Brighton on so many occasions and otherwise the game could have been over before the interval. First, he denied Diego Gómez from close range before stopping Yasin Ayari’s effort.

It has been revealed that two minutes later, Georginio Rutter was the next to be denied by the Greece international with another smart save before the pick of the bunch: Tzolakis made a reaction save with his foot to turn Gómez’s effort wide after Brighton cut Hull open at will again. At that stage it felt like when, not if, the visitors went ahead. Nobody told Tzolakis that.

Half-time did little to change the flow of momentum. Pascal Gross was next to be denied by Tzolakis before Gómez then shot wide from six yards out. At the other end, Hull were showing signs of coming to life, with two Mohamed Belloumi breaks a warning sign of what was to follow for the visitors.

Tzolakis was finally beaten by Charalampos Kostoulas when his chipped effort beat his fellow countryman, but Regan Slater was on hand to clear off the line. Then, as time ebbed away, Costinha’s second yellow decisively swung the momentum and within two minutes, Hull scored the goal Brighton had craved.

First, McBurnie bundled home before Belloumi’s break led to him squaring for the Scotland international to tap into an empty net. Was it what Brighton deserved? Probably not. But try persuading anyone of a Hull persuasion to care about that.

One of football's most-hyped 16-year-olds - what next for JJ Gabriel?
