📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MacBooks went to some adventurous new places this year. The MacBook Neo pushes the boundaries of how cheap and low-powered a MacBook could go, while the OLED MacBook Pro takes it in the opposite direction. While the midyear price hike put a damper on all the new releases, prices won’t be going down anytime soon.

Having tested every new MacBook you can buy, I can guide you to the right laptop for your budget and performance needs.

For more recommendations, check out the rest of our computer buying guides, like Best Laptops, Best Mac Desktops, Best Cheap Laptops, Best iPads, and Best MacBook Accessories.

Updated November 2026: I’ve added notes from my testing of the M6 MacBook Pro and OLED MacBook Pros, along with additional buying advice given the latest prices and rumors about future updates.

In a recent development, although the MacBook Neo is more affordable, and the M5 MacBook Pro offers a better display with the far more powerful M5 Pro and Max chips, the MacBook Air remains the model I recommend for most people. The 2026 M5 refresh isn’t particularly exciting, but if your livelihood depends on sitting in front of a MacBook all day, it’s the best option.

Sources indicate that the starting price for the 13-inch model is now $1,299, up $200 from before. Notably, for much of last year, you could buy this laptop for as little as $750. That’s a painful reality, but it doesn’t change my recommendation that this is the MacBook model most people should buy.

According to recent reports, although the exterior of the MacBook Air hasn’t changed since 2021, Apple has slowly evolved the laptop into something that feels airy and near-weightless. Most users need not worry about having too many tabs or applications open, eating up all that memory. You won’t be sitting around waiting for a file to download, because the SSD is blazing fast. With support for up to two 5K external monitors, the MacBook Air can function as a proper workstation when paired with a docking station. The 12-megapixel, 1080p webcam is plenty good for video calls.

In a recent development, what matters most is that the M5 can do far more than most people will ever ask of their MacBook Air. Apple has boosted the GPU so much over the past generations that the M5 is actually on par with the M3 Pro. You’ll probably spend most of your day in browser tabs, Slack, Zoom, office applications, and spreadsheets, but the MacBook Air can just as easily handle Photoshop or Lightroom. You can even dabble in video editing or some light gaming if you want. If you were a professional video editor, you’d likely be bothered by the render times. But if it’s more of a hobby or side project, the M5 MacBook Air likely won’t impede your flow. Again, that’s where the MacBook Air really lives up to its do-it-all reputation.

According to recent reports, as always, there are two sizes, measured diagonally: 13.6-inch and 15.3-inch. Aside from the $200 price gap, the screen size and speakers are the only notable differences between the two. Apple even scales up the pixel density to make sure the display on the 15-inch model looks just as sharp. The speakers on the 15-inch model sound incredible, second only to the 16-inch MacBook Pro. But choosing between the two sizes really comes down to how you use your laptop. If you have it plugged into an external monitor most days, you may as well get the 13-inch model and save yourself the extra space when you need to carry it around. But if a laptop is your primary machine, having that 15.3-inch screen really makes a difference, especially for more complicated applications or for using Split View.

In a recent development, as you may notice, the M5 MacBook Air now starts with 512 GB of storage. That’s twice what previous models packed and helps to rationalize the price gap between the Neo and the Air. Having 512 GB of storage means you won’t have to worry about filling up your drive right away. This kind of headroom allows the technology to fade into the background—a design philosophy Apple has always championed. If you are a power user, consider adding more memory. Remember, MacBook memory and internal storage aren’t expandable down the road.

Read my in-depth comparison of the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air to see how they stack up.

It has been revealed that after years of rumors, Apple has debuted a newly introduced MacBook Pro with never-before-seen features—most notably, the tandem PROLED XDR touchscreen. That’s right: this MacBook Pro is the first to ever have a touch-capable display, and you can now interact with it directly with your finger. Many people will be drawn in by the novelty of the feature (even though it’s been available on Windows laptops for almost a decade now), but I am skeptical about how useful it will be for day-to-day tasks. You will still primarily use the keyboard and trackpad, but I can see how the touchscreen would help in certain situations. Apple has made some optimizations to make the interface more touch-friendly, though I think there’s still room for improvement.

But don’t get me wrong: This MacBook Pro’s screen is the real deal. I’ve never seen a screen quite like this. Despite OLED’s reputation for not being bright enough, Apple’s is different. It delivers the insane contrast and clarity you’d expect from OLED, but with a maximum brightness that’s hundreds of nits higher than the previous-gen Mini-LED MacBook Pros.

Recent findings suggest that it has a few tricks up its sleeve too, such as the return of the glow-up Apple logo on the lid and the hole-punch camera to replace the notch. As someone who has never gotten used to that ugly notch, that might be the change I was most thrilled to see. Apple even brought Dynamic Island from the iPhone to the MacBook Pro, using that hole creatively while hiding the camera. All in all, there’s a lot to be impressed by here.

Recent findings suggest that the only real concern is that it still uses the older M5 Pro or M5 Max chip. These are still some of Apple’s most powerful chips, but they have been out for over a year. This is the first time Apple isn’t introducing latest chips alongside its new MacBook Pro in the past six years. Rumors indicate that the company may be skipping the M6 Pro and M6 Max altogether. That’s made stranger by the fact that Apple is keeping the previous-gen models in the lineup—another uncommon move.

There’s a $400 difference between the 2025 M5 Pro and the 2025 PROLED M5 Pro, and for this pro-level demographic of buyers, it’s a relatively small price to pay for all the upgrades. I appreciate that Apple kept the older models around for those who want the extra performance without the fancy, more expensive display. On the other hand, if Apple wasn’t presently selling them, third-party retailers might have dropped the price more while they were still in stock.

Sources indicate that the MacBook Neo (7/10, WIRED Recommends) came out earlier this year, and it had a lot to prove. That’s especially true since it debuted at just $599, an unheard-of price point for Apple laptops—much less than any other model, even before recent price hikes took effect. And even though the MacBook Neo now starts at $699 after those price increases, it remains an aggressively affordable option. To keep pricing low, Apple had to make the following compromises:.

Industry observers note that that’s a substantial list, and the memory limitation is the most significant drawback. Unlike on the MacBook Air, you can find the limits of the Neo fairly easily—and not on purpose. If you’re coming from a 16 GB MacBook Air, for example, you likely developed a habit of keeping idle applications or tabs open. On the MacBook Neo, you’ll need to be a bit more aware of what’s open to avoid slowdowns. You’ll also want to know which ports you’re using, since only the rear USB-C port supports an external display. The other USB-C port is only USB 2.0, rated at a max of 480 megabits per second. That’s definitely not the one you want to use for file transfers. If you don’t have the Touch ID model, you may even need to watch who you’re sitting next to in a coffee shop when entering passwords. We haven’t had to worry about these things on laptops for many years.

Industry observers note that in exchange, Apple delivers an incredible front-of-screen experience on the MacBook Neo, never before seen on a laptop of this price. The display is sharper and brighter than anything else you can buy for $699, while the keyboard and trackpad are both excellent. Build quality is every bit as strong as any other Apple product, and at 0.50 inches thick, it’s still quite portable.

On top of all that, the Neo has three really good features over the Air. There’s a wider range of color options—and a lot of people will gravitate toward the Neo for that alone. My favorite change is the lack of a camera notch. While the bezels are slightly thicker, I’d still prefer a uniform screen without an ugly notch blocking part of my view. Perhaps most meaningfully, the Neo is reportedly the most repairable MacBook in the lineup, swapping out adhesives for screws on components such as the battery and speakers. This is great for classrooms and businesses hoping to keep fleets of these up to date without contributing as much to the mounting e-waste problem.

It has been revealed that for most of the time, you’ll enjoy using the MacBook Neo. As a parent, this should be the go-to device for high school and college students. It also works equally well as a secondary laptop away from your workstation or as a small travel laptop.

Industry observers note that the newer PROLED MacBook Pros are flashier, but they use the same M5 Pro or M5 Max chips as the previous-gen models. And interestingly, Apple still sells these older ones. So, while these 2025 models don’t have touchscreen OLED displays, they’re every bit as powerful. You aren’t missing out on any performance, and if the rumors hold, these will be the top-of-the-line MacBook Pro chips for a while.

Of course, these MacBook Pros are still very expensive, though. Like its PROLED sibling, the standard M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro (8/10, WIRED Recommends) aren’t for the average person. The price alone should clue you in, but if you are the target audience and willing to pay well over $4,000 for a powerful laptop, the M5 Max MacBook Pro is unmatched in its capabilities. As always, the “Max” is primarily about considerably more GPU performance. Along with the option of two extra CPU cores, you can get up to 40 GPU cores, each with a built-in AI accelerator.

In a recent development, the M5 Max’s power applies to three use cases: creative applications, on-device AI processing, and gaming. Whether it’s 3D modeling, video editing, or some other resource-heavy application, the M5 Max MacBook Pro will tear through it. But AI performance also takes a significant leap. I tested a 17-billion-parameter Llama-2 model, which ran at conversational speed locally (the speed an AI model runs on a device), and it was 31 percent faster than running the same model on the M3 Max MacBook Pro.

Then there’s gaming. Nobody is going to buy the MacBook Pro for its gaming prowess alone, but it’s there when you want it. For the first time ever, you can hit over 60 frames per second in Cyberpunk 2077 on the Ultra preset with no upscaling. That’s an RTX 5070 Ti-level of laptop gaming performance. And unlike laptops that actually have that GPU, the MacBook Pro gets incredible battery life. Lastly, creative professionals will appreciate the faster storage speeds than previous generations.

The Mini-LED display is as gorgeous as ever, even if it pales in comparison to the fresh OLED models. You get a solid selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 5 ports that offer ample external display support. It’s at the top of its class in nearly every aspect. Beyond CPU/GPU performance, you can choose between two screen sizes that perform similarly.

Industry observers note that if this machine is overkill, you can drop down to the M5 Pro, which starts at $2,499 but is a power champ in its own right. Its multi-core and GPU performance are also stronger than the latest M6 (see below).

It has been revealed that the MacBook Pro is a slight misnomer because there are really three variants. I’ve talked about the PROLED and M5 Pro/M5 Max versions above. The third, the base model, is the new M6 MacBook Pro, and despite using the latest chip, it’s the cheapest of the Pro options. Unfortunately, it’s also the hardest to recommend. That has less to do with the laptop itself and more to do with its price and how it fits into the lineup.

Industry observers note that like its M5 predecessor, it remains a beautiful, well-made laptop with all the high-end features you’d expect from a MacBook Pro. That includes the excellent speakers and very bright Mini-LED display. But it costs $1,999. Keep in mind that the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is $2,499, and you can still buy the M5 model for $1,799 or the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air for $1,499—hence the “awkward middle child” designation.

According to recent reports, to be fair, you get a terabyte of storage and 16 GB of RAM, while the M5 MacBook Pro started with 512 GB of storage. Apple also kept the starting price the same—that is, the price after Apple increased pricing across the board (the base MacBook Pro used to start at $1,699), but let’s not go there.

In a recent development, the M6 chip is certainly faster than the M5, but it’s less of a substantial leap forward than in previous generations. You’re looking at about a 15 percent improvement in CPU performance. I think the bigger disappointment is only a 9 percent improvement in graphics. That’s been an area where previous generational chip leaps have been more significant.

Recent findings suggest that if you are considering the M6 MacBook Pro, I strongly suggest you look at the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air. It starts at a much lower price for the base configuration, but you can bump up the specs and still stay below $2,000. Yes, the MacBook Air is a different machine, but it has the performance that would impress many MacBook Pro customers.

All MacBooks were updated in 2026, making it a good time to buy one. The problem is that on June 25, Apple dramatically increased the price of all the MacBooks (and iPads) to varying degrees. Here’s a breakdown of the fresh starting prices, with increases ranging from $100 to $400:.

It’s rare for Apple to raise prices suddenly, especially when the change doesn’t coincide with a product refresh. What made this revision especially unusual, though, is that only a few months had passed since the MacBook Neo launched. Apple blamed the price spikes on memory and storage increases, stating that AI data centers had “created an extraordinary surge in demand” never seen before.

In a recent development, so yes, the better time to buy a MacBook would have been earlier this year. While Apple says that it is “working tirelessly to find solutions,” I wouldn’t expect these prices to come down anytime soon. Predictions around how long this memory shortage will last are measured in years, not months.

Right now, only the 14-inch MacBook Pro gets the latest M6 chip. Rumors suggest Apple will skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max in this generation, saving the chip update for the MacBook Pro until the M7 Pro and M7 Max.

A Breakdown of Each M-Series Chip.

Apple’s processors are scattered across different MacBook models, and you can find older models online from third-party retailers, either new or refurbished. If you do stumble upon older chips, you might be wondering how they compare to newer options. Here, get a breakdown of the differences to consider.

In a recent development, M6: Apple has already released its latest M6 line of chips, though the rollout has been slower than normal. As of this year, it’s only available in the base 14-inch MacBook Pro, iMac, and Mac Mini. I expect to see this arrive on devices like the iPad Pro and MacBook Air eventually, but the rumors about the rest of the M6 lineup are perplexing. Reports indicate Apple will skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max entirely and jump straight to the M7 Pro and M7 Max, perhaps in late 2027. That makes sense given what Apple just launched with the OLED MacBook Pro, which uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the previous generation.

Recent findings suggest that M5: Apple launched the M5 chips in late 2025 with the 14-inch MacBook Pro, iPad Pro, and Vision Pro. The base M5 offers up to a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, though a lower-tier 9-core CPU is still available on the iPad Pro. The M5 is about 10 to 15 percent faster in CPU performance than the M4 and takes a significant step up in GPU, AI workloads, and even storage speed. The M5 is now also available on the MacBook Air.

M5 Pro: These more powerful M5 chips are at the moment available in the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros. The M5 Pro comes with a 15-core CPU and a 16-core GPU, with an option to upgrade to an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU. As with previous generations, the Pro chip gets all the same benefits as those in the M5 architecture but adds more cores and improved memory bandwidth. The biggest advantage is in GPU and on-device AI performance. This time around, however, both the M5 Pro and M5 Max also debuted the “Fusion Architecture,” a new version of UltraFusion (previously used only on the Ultra chips) that combines two dies across a superfast interconnect.

M5 Max: The M5 Max is the M5 Pro—only with more GPU power. You can get up to 40 GPU cores, putting the MacBook Pro on par with high-end gaming laptops in graphics performance. With neural accelerators built into each GPU core, you’ve got one of the most powerful AI laptops on the market. It comes in either the MacBook Pro or the Mac Studio.

M5 Ultra: Like the other “Ultra” chips, the M5 Ultra is available only in the 2026 Mac Studio. It’s by far Apple’s most powerful chip, but you can’t configure it in a MacBook.

M4: The M4 debuted in 2024. It has a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU. Apple claims the M4 delivers 1.8 times faster CPU performance and 2.2 times faster GPU performance than the M1. Meanwhile, the neural engine is more than three times faster than the original and twice as fast as the M3. It also starts with 16 GB of unified memory, which helps to power Apple Intelligence (the company’s suite of artificial intelligence features) more smoothly. It’s available on the 14-inch MacBook Pro (2024), iMac (2024), and MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, 2025).

In a recent development, M4 Pro: The M4 Pro has a 14-core CPU (which Apple claims is up to 1.9 times faster than the M1 Pro) and up to a 20-core GPU, with up to 64 GB of unified memory. Built on a second-generation 3-nanometer process, it also supports enhanced GPU features like mesh shading and ray tracing—the latter of which is now twice as fast as on M3 chips. You’ll find it on the 2024 MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) and Mac Mini (2024).

M4 Max: This chip has a 16-core CPU and up to a 40-core GPU with support for up to 128 GB of unified memory. Apple notes the CPU is up to 2.2 times faster than the M1 Max, while the GPU is up to 1.9 times faster. Like the M4 Pro, it supports mesh shading and ray tracing. The M4 Max is available as an option on the 2024 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro, and you can also get it as an option in the current Mac Studio.

Industry observers note that M3: The M3 was available on the 14-inch MacBook Pro (late 2023), 13-inch MacBook Air (2024), 15-inch MacBook Air (2024), and 24-inch iMac (2023). It packs an 8-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, with up to 24 GB of unified memory. Compared with the M1, Apple claimed CPU performance was up to 35 percent faster and GPU performance up to 65 percent faster. The company said the CPU and GPU are both 20 percent faster than the M2. As with the M1 and M2, it was great for basic tasks like word processing, sending emails, using spreadsheets, and light gaming. The 13-inch and 15-inch MacBook Air also supported two external displays (one up to 6K at 60 Hz and another up to 5K at 60 Hz).

According to recent reports, M3 Pro: With a 12-core CPU and an 18-core GPU, Apple claimed the M3 Pro’s GPU was only up to 10 percent faster than the M2 Pro, making it a marginal upgrade from its predecessor. Compared with the M1 Pro, however, the M2 Pro was up to 40 percent faster in GPU performance and 20 percent faster in CPU performance. It was available on the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro from 2023. It was the ideal in-between for those who needed a chip more powerful than the M3 but didn’t need the full power of the M3 Max.

M3 Max: The next step up from the M2 Max. It had a 16-core CPU, 40-core GPU, and up to 128 GB of unified memory. According to Apple, the CPU performance was up to 80 percent faster than the M1 Max and up to 50 percent faster than the M2 Max. As for GPU performance, it was remarked to be up to 50 percent faster than the M1 Max and 20 percent faster than the M2 Max. The M3 Max was available on the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro (late 2023).

It has been revealed that M3 Ultra: Apple introduced the M3 lineup in 2023, but only revealed the M3 Ultra in 2025. It was even better than the latest M4 Max and M5 at the time. It had up to 32 CPU cores (24 performance cores) and up to 80 GPU cores. Apple claimed it was up to 2.5 times faster than the M1 Ultra. It also came with 96 GB of unified memory, upgradable to 512 GB, and up to 16 TB of SSD storage. This chip was available only on the 2025 Mac Studio.

M2: The M2 was an entry-level chip like the M1, with slightly more processing power. It packed an 8-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU (two more GPU cores than its predecessor), and supported up to 24 GB of unified memory. Apple stated the second-generation chip has an 18 percent faster CPU and a GPU that’s 35 percent more powerful than its earlier version. The M2 was great for daily tasks like word processing and web browsing, but tasks such as editing multiple streams of 4K footage and 3D rendering should be reserved for Pro or Max chips. It was available in the MacBook Air (13-inch, 2022), MacBook Air (15-inch, 2022), and MacBook Pro (13-inch, 2022).

M2 Pro: The M2 Pro had up to 12 cores in the CPU and up to a 19-core GPU, with up to 32 GB of unified memory. Apple claimed performance was up to 20 percent faster than with the 10-core M1 Pro and graphics were 30 percent faster. We recommended this chip for intermediate video and photo editors. It was a marginal upgrade compared with the M1 Pro, but it was the best option for those who wanted a more future-proof processor. You could find it in the MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) from early 2023 and the Mac Mini (2023).

M2 Max: The M2 Max packs up to a 12-core CPU and up to a 38-core GPU (with support for up to 96 GB of unified memory). According to Apple, graphics are 30 percent faster than on the M1 Max. The M2 Max is an excellent choice for those who work with graphics-intensive content, including graphic design, 3D modeling, and heavy-duty video footage. But as with the M2 Pro, it’s an incremental upgrade if you’re coming from an M1 Max. It’s available in the MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) released in early 2023 and the Mac Studio (2023).

Recent findings suggest that M2 Ultra: The successor to the M1 Ultra, the M2 Ultra was available in the second-generation Mac Studio and the Mac Pro (2023). Composed of two M2 Max chips, using Apple’s UltraFusion technology, the M2 Ultra had a 24-core CPU and a GPU configurable with 60 or 76 cores. Apple claimed the CPU delivered up to 20 percent faster performance and that the GPU was up to 30 percent faster than the M1 Ultra. This was the chip to get if you were working with extremely heavy-duty content that you believed the M1 Ultra, M2 Pro, or M2 Max simply couldn’t handle. You’d have known if you needed a chip this robust.

Sources indicate that M1: Introduced in 2020, the M1 was Apple's first custom silicon designed for the Mac. The M1 had an 8-core CPU and up to an 8-core GPU. Originally, you could get up to 16 GB of unified memory (RAM) for an extra cost, but now you can only purchase the 8-GB model. It was much faster than any previous Intel-powered MacBook Pro and the practical choice for most people. It packed more than enough processing power for day-to-day tasks and even light gaming. It could also handle more intense jobs, like photo editing. Long after its initial release, Apple continued to sell the M1 MacBook Air through Walmart for just $599, a killer price for this laptop. The MacBook Neo has since replaced it, using the A18 Pro chip from the iPhone 16 Pro models.

In a recent development, M1 Pro: The next step up was the M1 Pro. It had up to 10 CPU cores and up to a 16-core GPU, with up to 32 GB of unified memory. Apple said the performance and graphics were both twice as fast as on the M1. We found it to be considerably more capable than the base chip, making it ideal for anyone who works heavily on MacBooks for music production or photo and video editing. Only the 2021 MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) used this chip.

M1 Max: Like the M1 Pro, the M1 Max had a 10-core CPU but a heftier 32-core GPU (with support for up to 64 GB of unified memory). Apple said it was four times faster than the M1 for graphics. As testing highlighted, this chip was extremely powerful and handled every heavy-duty task with ease. It was the go-to choice if you needed a computer that could handle multiple streams of 8K or 4K video footage, 3D rendering, or app development and demos. You probably already knew whether you needed this much power. It was available in the MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) from 2021.

M1 Ultra: The M1 Ultra was the most powerful of the M1 series. It’s two M1 Max chips connected with a technology called UltraFusion. It packs a 20-core CPU, 64-core GPU (configurable up to 128 GB of unified memory), and a 32-core neural engine—complete with seven times more transistors than the base M1. Even when newer models were available, the M1 Ultra remained powerful and a solid option for anyone who needs a heavy-duty processor for intense visuals and graphics work. It was available only on the first-generation Mac Studio.

Which MacBooks Are Compatible With macOS 27 Golden Gate?

macOS 27 Golden Gate is the latest version of the operating system that runs on MacBooks. The patch focuses on beefing up Siri, now integrated into Spotlight search. It also has a dedicated Siri AI app that works more like the AI chatbots we’re all so familiar with these days. This all-encompassing perspective of Apple Intelligence is even integrated into Finder and the right-click menu.

Notably, macOS 27 Golden Gate is the first version to drop support for pre-2020 Macs with Intel processors. The following Mac models will receive Apple’s enhancement to macOS 27 Golden Gate:.

Industry observers note that the previous version of macOS is Tahoe (or macOS 26), which came out in September of 2025. The software brought a host of newly introduced features, including a visual redesign, a spruced-up Spotlight, and a new Games app.

Which Macs Support Apple Intelligence?

Apple launched the first set of Apple Intelligence features with macOS Sequoia 15.1, including Writing Tools, an overhauled Siri, Smart Replies, Mail Summaries, and Clean Up in Photos. However, Apple Intelligence is exclusive to Macs with an M-series chip. This includes the following:.

Get AppleCare+ to Protect Your Devices.

It has been revealed that none of Apple’s MacBooks are cheap, and replacement parts are nightmarishly expensive. Since the entire computer is fully integrated into Apple’s tightly designed aluminum chassis, you’re one coffee spill away from a shockingly large repair bill. This makes AppleCare+ worth buying. Remember, you have to purchase it within 60 days of buying your MacBook.

Apple offers monthly or yearly payments. Both include unlimited accidental protection along with 24/7 telephone support. If your MacBook has screen or enclosure damage, you’ll pay a $99 service fee; other accidental damage costs $299. The monthly payments vary depending on the specific MacBook you buy:.

Take Advantage of Apple’s Education Discounts.

In a recent development, apple always offers small discounts on hardware for students and teachers. To access the deals, purchase through Apple’s Education Store, choose the product you want (you should see the discounted pricing), and place the order as you normally would. You don’t need to show proof that you’re a student at the time of purchase, but be honest, as Apple can ask for verification later. It’s worth noting that the discounts are not as good as what you’ll find on Amazon and sometimes at other retailers like Walmart, so be sure to check prices.

You have to be very careful when shopping for older MacBooks. Don’t get me wrong: Since the introduction of Apple Silicon in 2020, almost every MacBook Air and MacBook Pro has been a really good laptop. Never buy a MacBook that predates 2020, regardless of how cheap it is. Trust me.

It has been revealed that but even buying an older Apple Silicon model requires a discerning eye. Most older generations of MacBooks are sold only refurbished or secondhand, which adds risk. Meanwhile, prices on refurbished models fluctuate frequently, so you’ll need to watch prices closely to get the best deal. Apple’s own refurbished store prices are often higher than buying latest models from third-party retailers like Amazon or Best Buy, but you do get some protection as they come with an Apple warranty. However, third-party retailers are always less risky than buying used on a secondhand market like Facebook Marketplace or eBay.

With that in mind, here are the older MacBooks you might see for sale, and whether I’d recommend buying.

In a recent development, macBook Pro (M5): Apple doesn’t sell this one anymore, but some retailers are selling it at a discount for $1,799. That’s for 16 GB of RAM and a terabyte of storage. Since it’s nearly identical to the newer M6 MacBook Pro, except for a small performance bump, it’s a really good deal right now. I’d still say most people are better off getting a 15-inch MacBook Air because it’s cheaper and thinner, but if you want the better Mini-LED display, the M5 MacBook Pro is a solid choice right now.

MacBook Air (M4): The previous-generation MacBook Air is a fantastic laptop, but it’s no longer being sold upcoming. However, you can now buy it refurbished for under $1,000. This configuration only comes with 256 GB of storage, though, and I don’t think it’s cheap enough to be worth it compared to the M5 model.

MacBook Air (M3): This one isn’t being sold new anymore, and the refurbished models I could find weren’t any cheaper than the M4 MacBook Air. Just stick with the M4.

MacBook Air (M2): With the launch of the MacBook Neo, there’s really no reason to buy an older MacBook Air with only 8 GB of RAM—especially at this price.

MacBook Air (M1): Thanks to the Neo, refurbished M1 MacBook Air models have sunk to pretty dramatic lows. You can currently buy a refurbished M1 for around $400. While the M1 MacBook Air gets you a backlit keyboard, the new MacBook Neo is certainly the more handsome and portable of the two. Still, if you need something fairly limited and are willing to risk buying refurbished, I can see why an Apple Silicon MacBook for less than $400 has its appeal.

According to recent reports, macBook Pro (14-inch, M4): This is no longer being sold new, but you can buy the refurbished model for $1,499. Earlier this year, you could have bought the M5 model for less than this. Sigh. Even still—definitely not worth it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This most unpredictable and evenly contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive defeat, by virtue of a terrific performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places.

The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool. It was the first time City had failed to win a home league match during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16 months in charge, let alone lose.

Nevertheless, the victory was fully deserved for Tottenham, who made Khadija “Bunny” Shaw wait to equal her teammate Vivianne Miedema’s all-time WSL goalscoring record of 97 goals.

In a recent development, jeglertz described the defeat as a “wake-up call” for his team, adding: “Tottenham were a little bit more urgent than us. Each duel counts, each moment counts, each ball counts. That was something that I missed with our players, especially in the second half where we needed to score and we needed to beat them in one-versus-one situations. I missed a little bit of that urgency, which I think is the most key in a team, and if we drop a little bit in that, this league is so tight and tough and the teams are so good, you will drop points and lose games.”.

Before the game, the anticipated storyline felt almost too obvious. Shaw, needing three goals to surpass Miedema, was facing a club against whom she had scored four hat-tricks, including on Tottenham’s most recent visit to this stadium in March, when she recorded the WSL’s fastest treble. Persistently their tormentor, Shaw has scored more goals against Spurs than any other player has managed against a single opponent in the competition.

When Shaw opened the scoring inside 10 minutes, everything seemed to be following the script. Jade Rose, pressing very high up the pitch for a centre-back, won the ball and played a precise low pass across to Shaw, who tucked into the bottom corner from inside the box to record her 96th WSL goal and her 16th against Tottenham.

Sources indicate that that, however, proved to be the only effort at goal – on or off target – that City would register during the opening 45 minutes, as Tottenham impressed. Kirsty Hanson drew a good save from Ayaka Yamashita and Hanson also felt she had a very strong claim for a penalty when Carlotta Wamser appeared to foul her inside the area, but it was not long before the visitors were deservedly level as Cathinka Tandberg expertly turned home Hanson’s cross with a clinical near-post finish.

Tottenham continued to threaten after the break, although Rose scooped over the bar to spurn a huge City chance on the rebound after a Lauren Hemp free-kick had been parried by Lize Kop. Some very effective counterattacking football then deservedly won the game for Tottenham as they scored twice to stun the defending champions.

First, in the 74th minute, an exquisite Drew Spence through ball found the run of Matilda Vinberg – who was a late addition to the starting side after the withdrawal of Olivia Holdt during the warm-up because of stomach pains – and Vinberg revealed her quality to turn Rose and fire past Yamashita. Vinberg turned provider five minutes later, to set up Jessica Naz for another good finish.

Martin Ho, the Tottenham head coach, hailed his team’s “outstanding” display, saying: “Every time we play a team who has been in the top three consistently, the conversation is: ‘Can you get one over the line?’ And, for the players, they need to feel what that feels like and enjoy that. Today we nullified a lot of their threats. That will give us a lot of confidence.”.

Manchester City had won 12 of their 13 previous WSL games against Tottenham, and all of their past 17 WSL home games, but this defeat added a further dent to their title challenge after their loss at Stamford Bridge last weekend. Chelsea, held to a goalless draw by Liverpool on Saturday, remain two points clear.

It has been revealed that arsenal remain winless at home in the WSL this season after being held to another frustrating draw at the Emirates, this time by West Ham. Arsenal had 22 shots at goal but were unable to break the deadlock, as their under-pressure head coach, Renée Slegers, oversaw a sixth home league draw out of six, leaving Arsenal eight points behind the top three.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United left it late to come from behind and beat Birmingham 2-1 but Simi Awujo’s last-gasp header from a corner gave them a valuable win and extended Eva Olid’s side’s club-record unbeaten run to 14 matches in all competitions. Birmingham had led inside four minutes through Lee Geum-min’s expert volley but Elisabeth Terland’s close-range finish with 10 minutes to go and Awujo’s 94th-minute winner snatched it, moving Olid’s fourth-placed team just six points off the top.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, the bottom side Charlton collected their first point of the season as they drew 1-1 with Aston Villa, while Brighton moved into the top half with a 1-0 victory at Everton, courtesy of Maz Pacheco’s early own goal. Tom Garry.

According to recent reports, jeglertz continued: “We will bounce back, I’m not worried about that. I know the qualities in this group. But it’s the good habits, the small details that matter. Those are the things that win titles – this was actually the first time that I missed that in a game and I’m pretty sure it’s not going to happen again.” With just seven points now separating the top five, his team can ill-afford for it to happen again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on Thursday, the immersive entertainment technology manufacturer revealed a new studio partnership with The Walt Disney Co. that will bring the original "Star Wars" to its domes early next year as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration.

The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Cosm's massive concave screens will drop film fans into a galaxy far, far away starting in March, just ahead of the Academy Award-winning film's 50th anniversary in May.

"We are thrilled to add the Disney partnership," Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. "We do look for those opportunities of these like anniversary and commemorative moments. We look for those opportunities to celebrate with the fans, but also find this mutually beneficial partnership between both parties.".

This will be Cosm's sixth theatrical collaboration with Hollywood, having already partnered with Warner Bros. to bring "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. The manufacturer is set to launch immersive screenings of Universal's "Shrek" in December.

Each Cosm dome has stadium-style seating, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width fills much of the viewers' periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the onscreen environment.

It has been revealed that in this case, "Star Wars" will be displayed in a large rectangle in the center of the dome while the background is transformed into the iconic planets of Tatooine and Yavin IV that are featured in the film as well as the infamous Death Star. Audiences will also see elements that will make it appear like they're traveling at lightspeed and getting trapped in an intergalactic trash compactor.

Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for the unique presentation of the film.

Sources indicate that "We look for those moments where sound, music ... listening to Darth Vader's breath for the first time ... you feel those moments differently in an 87-foot diameter dome and 12k resolution with the sound system we have," Scalice said. "And it's one of the things that with experiential cinema and our technology that we were so excited and honestly privileged that we can take these defining moments for fans and work closely with our partners that doesn't really change the authenticity of it, it just enhances it in a different manner.".

The premium experience will also be paired with a themed menu. Cosm has done this with other titles, such as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," serving guests throughout the screening with house-made shepherd's pie, pretzel wands with cheese dip and a box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans.

Cosm is trying to establish itself as a destination for fandom — both for sports and for film. It has a wide variety of live event offerings, which it telecasts using proprietary cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, as well as its expanding library of movies.

"What I love is that we really are kind of building these Cosm communities built on fandom," Scalice said. "It's the No. 1 foundation for our business.".

It has been revealed that and Star Wars is a powerful fandom. The franchise remains one of the top-ranking pieces of intellectual property across film, television and retail annually, and Disney is gearing up for a massive celebration of its semicentennial including merchandise rolls out, theatrical re-releases, its biannual Star Wars Celebration convention and collaborations with other brands.

Correction: This story has been updated to correct the spelling of Alexis Scalice's name.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, some VIP Twitter users woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously declared purge by Elon Musk.
  • In a recent development, twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on April 1.
  • But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Upcoming York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some VIP Twitter users woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously declared purge by Elon Musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

In a recent development, twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on April 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Upcoming York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

It has been revealed that william Shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue Twitter checkmark. Elon Musk notes too bad.

After an account that often engages with Musk posted a meme this weekend about the Times declining to pay for verification, Musk responded in a tweet saying, “Oh ok, we’ll take it off then.” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda.”.

In a recent development, the weekend moves are just the latest example of Twitter creating confusion and whiplash for users over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

Although the Newly introduced York Times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post.) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not plan to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a recent development, in a separate puzzling move, Twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on Monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which Musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from consumers verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

Sources indicate that in early November, Twitter launched the option for people paying for its Twitter Blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was swiftly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual customers would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent consumers such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

Sources indicate that by muddying the reason accounts are verified, the latest label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile customers. Experts in inauthentic behavior have also said it’s not clear that reserving verification for paid users will reduce the number of bots on the site, an glitch Musk has raised on and off over the past year.

Musk, for his part, has previously presented changes to Twitter’s verification system as a way of “treating everyone equally.”.

“There shouldn’t be a different standard for celebrities,” he mentioned in a tweet last week. The paid feature could also drive revenue, which could help Musk, who is on the hook for significant debt after buying Twitter for $44 billion.

Musk last week also said that starting on April 15, only verified accounts would be recommended in people’ “For You” feeds alongside the accounts they follow.

–CNN’s Oliver Darcy contributed to this report.

This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.
  • “Don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” Bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to Glasgow.
  • A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthony Bourdain loved haggis. But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.

“Don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” Bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to Glasgow. “There is no more unfairly reviled food on Earth than the haggis.”.

A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.

Industry observers note that instagrammable is not the word that immediately comes to mind. In our 21st-century world, where “clean” eating and processed pap overlap, haggis can seem like an “Outlander”-style outlier from another age.

Yet, by some alchemy, once cooked to its required “warm-reekin’ (steaming)” state, it adds up to much more than the sum of its modest parts. It’s offaly charm has kept nose-to-tail eating alive among a younger generation of Scots that has largely turned its back on the tripe, liver and kidneys their predecessors enjoyed (or endured).

Carefully prepared, haggis tastes both oaty and meaty; it is dark and crumbly, a little crispy at the edges but still moist; earthy but also savory and spicy; deep-tasting and profoundly warming, the perfect foil for its traditional garnish of floury mashed potatoes and orange bashed turnip.

“It’s like a cuddle for the stomach,” indicates Nicola Turner, a 35-year-old office administrator from Helensburgh, a town on western Scotland’s Firth of Clyde.

For children of the 1960s and ’70s, like crime novelist Ian Rankin, haggis meals were a choice between the classic meat-and-two-veg plate and the battered and deep-fried, chip-shop iteration loved by both his friend Bourdain and his quintessentially Scottish detective character, Inspector John Rebus.

Now myriad other treatments have blossomed.

Sources indicate that “I’m pretty sure the first time I dined with AB in Edinburgh we had haggis in filo pastry with a jam-style – maybe blackcurrant – sauce,” Rankin recalled. “He was a major fan of haggis and of chip shops. Rebus will have enjoyed the occasional haggis supper from his local chip shop. He was definitely a fan, as am I.”.

Industry observers note that “It is all about the spicing and the texture,” notes the Scottish food writer, novelist and cook Sue Lawrence, a champion of haggis’ adaptability for use in other dishes. “If you didn’t know what was in it, you wouldn’t think ‘oh that tastes of liver or whatever.’ It is all nicely chopped up and the oatmeal gives it a lovely texture. It could easily be a nice, big mince dish.”.

These US restaurants and chefs are James Beard Award finalists.

Recent findings suggest that lawrence uses haggis as an alternative to beef and pork ragù in lasagna and in her pastilla, a version of the North African dish in which a hand-made haggis from the Isle of Mull substitutes for the traditional poultry or seafood filling. The filo pastry savory is flavored with the spice blend ras el hanout, apricots, chile, orange zest and almonds before being sprinkled with cinnamon and icing sugar.

Such cultural crossovers serve as a reminder that haggis could easily be a dish with nothing specifically Scottish about it at all. Records of similar quick and portable preparations of the fast-perishing innards of sheep and other animals date back to ancient Rome and Greece.

Haggis-like combinations of offal and grains are part of the culinary history of several countries. Spain has chireta, Romania drob and Sweden polsa, while chaudin, or ponce, is a rice and meat-stuffed pig stomach that is a staple of Cajun cooking.

In neighboring England, recipes for “hagese,” “hagws of a schepe,” “haggas” or “haggus” pop up in recipe books published between the 15th and 17th centuries, probably preceding written records north of the border.

Etymological evidence points to the term “haggis” having its roots in Old Norse, suggesting an early version of an oat-and-offal sausage might have arrived in Britain and Ireland on a Viking longboat.

But ever since it was first optioned by the poet Robert Burns in the late 1700s, the haggis backstory has been monopolized by Scotland and the Scots, sometimes mischievously.

It is, according to the kind of lore that Burns engendered, the dish a doughty Highlander would carry with him as he drove cattle through the glens to the markets of the central belt or the perfect picnic for a whisky smuggler plying his illicit trade by moonlight.

It has been revealed that from such romantic notions it was a short step to turning the haggis into a wee wild beastie, one with longer legs on one side that was thus condemned to run round and round whichever hill it lived on. In 2003, a poll of American tourists in Scotland found that one in three of them believed they might encounter such a confused creature on a Caledonian vacation.

Bourdain, a native New Yorker, may have qualified as haggis’ biggest admirer since Burns, but his compatriots at the US Department of Agriculture remain unconverted to offal-filled paunch. Haggis imports into the United States were prohibited in 1971 as part of a ban on the consumption of all livestock lungs. Authentic versions of old school haggis remain culinary contraband in the US, as hard to lay your hands on as Cuban cigars.

Across the rest of the world, it’s a different story. According to leading producer Simon Howie, haggis is more widely appreciated and consumed now than it has been since Burns improvised his “Address to a Haggis” for the entertainment of well-to-do Edinburgh acquaintances.

Firmly tongue-in-cheek, the poem lauds the “Great chieftain o’ the pudding race,” as exactly the kind of unpretentious, hearty fare required to nourish a nation of braveheart warriors.

In comparison to the enfeebling foreign muck enjoyed by the capital’s claret-quaffing elites of the time – the olio, fricassée or ragoût that would “sicken a sow” – Burns urges his readers to wonder at the magical impact of haggis on his fellow sons of Scotland’s soil.

As the English translation of the original Scots language version puts it:.

But mark the Rustic, haggis-fed/.

The trembling earth resounds his tread/.

Clap in his ample fist a blade/.

And legs and arms and heads will cut/.

These days synthetic casings have largely replaced stomach but ovine and porcine innards remain at the core of most of the haggis produced in its homeland, remarked Howie, who estimates that his company Simon Howie Butchers, accounts for around 60% of the roughly two million haggises produced every year.

Sources indicate that for Howie, versatility, value for money and convenience explain why this staple of the Scottish larder is thriving. Typically haggis retails in Scotland, which accounts for half of global consumption by volume, for around £6, or $7.70 per kilogram ($3.36/pound). That’s around half the price of less expensive cuts of beef or a third of the price of Scotch lamb while enjoying a fairly similar nutritional and calorific profile.

Best Mexican food: 23 dishes to try.

“You can give your kids a meal that is not full of things you don’t want to feed them – for a few pounds you can feed three strapping lads,” Howie mentioned.

Industry observers note that “From a kitchen perspective, it is very simple because when it leaves our factory it is already cooked. So when you or a restaurant owner gets it into the kitchen all you have to do is heat it up to be piping hot. It couldn’t be more basic: a student with no cooking skills or a Michelin-starred chef do exactly the same thing to put it out on the plate.”.

Its texture means haggis can also be usefully deployed in fine dining alongside leaner meat like venison or as a stuffing for poultry and game birds. Its spicy intensity means it is also finding uses in canapés and as a crouton-borne garnish for soups.

Buoyant sales are also underpinned by the increasing consumption of haggis in forms inspired by Scotland’s ethnic minorities.

Glasgow’s Sikh community pioneered haggis pakora in the 1990s and samosas, spring rolls and quesadillas have followed in its wake, often using a vegetarian version of the protein in which the offal is replaced by a mix of vegetables, pulses and mushrooms.

Sources indicate that such dishes are more than culinary twists. They are badges of belonging, and an indication that, two centuries after Burns grabbed it for the nation, haggis is as intimately entwined with Scots identity as ever.

Just ask Ross O’Cinneide, a promising 14-year-old fly-half in the junior section of Stirling County rugby club.

In a recent development, “Most of my friends and I like haggis,” he indicates. “Mum makes it for us sometimes after rugby and it’s got a very nice warming feeling. And it’s nice because it’s purely Scottish.”.

Breaking: Retailers are turning to entertainment to win shoppers’ attention

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • made an unconventional hire earlier this year: a chief entertainment officer.
  • According to recent reports, it was a newly created role as the company tapped former Paramount executive Pam Kaufman to helm its entertainment, content and licensing platform.
  • Sources indicate that "Beloved brands have value beyond the products they sell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Legacy retailer Gap Inc. made an unconventional hire earlier this year: a chief entertainment officer.

According to recent reports, it was a newly created role as the company tapped former Paramount executive Pam Kaufman to helm its entertainment, content and licensing platform. Gap has since rolled out major campaigns, partnering with bands like Just Your Type and building on the success of last year's ads with girl group Katseye.

Sources indicate that "Beloved brands have value beyond the products they sell. Consumers identify with them, trust them and want to be part of their world," Kaufman told CNBC in a statement. "The key is authenticity: Every extension has to reflect what the brand stands for and give its fans a meaningful newly introduced way to experience it.".

She said it's part of a broader goal to emphasize what Gap calls "fashiontainment," a strategy to blend retail and entertainment to better align with consumers. Gap is part of a growing cohort of retailers investing in entertainment and experiences both in-store and through exclusive online content to drive engagement.

"Brands are stories, and we are the storytellers," CEO Richard Dickson stated at the Goldman Sachs Global Consumer and Retail conference in September. "I think you could see that come to life when you look at some of the work that we've done, putting our brands in the center of culture and cultural conversation.".

According to recent reports, in another blending of retail and media, Mattel made waves a few years ago for its "Barbie" movie, building on the intellectual property of a decades-old fan favorite and drawing in massive box office success. At the time, Dickson was president and chief operating officer of the firm, witnessing firsthand the sectors' intersection before departing for Gap.

"I think the post-Covid consumer attitude around shopping certainly evolved a lot," remarked Bryan Eshelman, who leads the retail practice at consulting firm AlixPartners. "It has gone from shopping as a fulfillment task to shopping, in many instances, more as an entertainment form.".

Between experiences in physical stores and media campaigns featuring exclusive content, Eshelman stated, retailers are getting more creative about the ways they're driving engagement and marketing.

"Community, at the end of the day, is one of the key ways to drive loyalty, so I think retailers of all types are trying to tap into some sense of community, some sense of lifestyle, some sense of belonging that's beyond the product that they offer," he said.

Branded entertainment has been around for a long time. Procter & Gamble made headlines in the 1930s for helping to coin the term "soap opera," and companies have for decades created media campaigns to draw in customers.

But with the rise of social media, content creation and short-form offerings, experts said audiences are becoming hungrier than ever for something latest and original.

The retail and entertainment intersection is happening at a time when intellectual property is becoming more valuable than ever, according to experts.

As consumers encounter more marketing than ever, the companies that will win the battle for attention are the ones that can "cut through all of the noise," said Alex Michael, senior managing director at investment firm LionTree.

"The hardest thing to find and to get is audience these days," Michael told CNBC. "IP, in that sense, is the most valuable thing out there, and only becoming more valuable because it's attached to audience.".

It has been revealed that at the same time, he said, the way IP is distributed is broadening to include video, audio, short-form, long-form and live event content. Consumers are also redefining their loyalty to brands, which means companies have to "play much earlier in the consumer journey" than they have in years past to secure their trust, he said.

The trend is also likely helped by executives who have worked in both retail and entertainment: Gap's Kaufman came from Paramount, for example, and Dickson and Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz held top roles at Mattel.

Recent findings suggest that "The gray areas have never been more pronounced as to what is classically defined as retail or media or entertainment or live events," Michael noted. "People who have cross-sector expertise are increasingly more valuable because you can't be defined by a single vertical, especially as things change so quickly.".

Still, there's room for newer players, especially with the studio landscape rapidly changing, said Sean Akaks, the CEO of SonderCo, an agency that partners brands with celebrities and entertainment properties.

In a recent development, "I think it's a really interesting time for nontraditional players to be making content because you're seeing this massive consolidation of these legacy entertainment companies," he said. "I think there are just more open lanes for independent creators and also brands and anyone outside the traditional studio system to create content.".

That's where retailers might tap creators, Akaks said, because they can use their platforms to reach consumers directly.

"I do think there's a world where we're going to see creators and brands sort of co-creating IP that maybe they're owning together," he noted.

Once those companies get consumers into the store, they're also leaning into experiential retail, making shopping a more immersive experience than it otherwise would be, like Dick's Sporting Goods offering interactive activities and simulators in its stores.

According to data from AlixPartners, companies investing in experiential retail such as Coach and Ralph Lauren saw close to 10% year-over-year increases in consumers' average basket size.

"The idea that retailers would potentially invest in some distributed electronic content to help drive traffic, and then when you get there, it's experiential — it really goes into the kinds of flywheels that entertainment companies are also trying to build and grow," remarked Jeff Goldstein, co-lead of the media and entertainment practice at AlixPartners.

Sources indicate that yet, the entertainment that retail brands are developing is only one piece in a larger puzzle to retain customers and attract new ones. Translating that into tangible sales growth isn't necessarily a given.

According to recent reports, "The basics of having great product in stock at a transparent price that feels like value is not swept away by animatronics," AlixPartners' Eshelman noted. "The fundamentals are still there, and if you're going to have a good retail proposition, you need to have that balance. You can't mask bad product at a bad price with no inventory with glitz and glamour.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Kwame Brathwaite, the pioneering activist and photographer whose work helped define the aesthetics of the “Black is Beautiful” movement of the 1960s and beyond, died on April 1, aged 85.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  This article was originally published by The Art Newspaper, an editorial partner of CNN Style.

Kwame Brathwaite, the pioneering activist and photographer whose work helped define the aesthetics of the “Black is Beautiful” movement of the 1960s and beyond, died on April 1, aged 85.

His son, Kwame Brathwaite, Jr, announced his father’s death in an Instagram post that read in part, “I am deeply saddened to share that my Baba, the patriarch of our family, our rock and my hero has transitioned.”.

Brathwaite’s work has been the subject of resurgent interest from curators, historians and collectors in recent years, and his first major institutional retrospective, which was organized by the Aperture Foundation, made its debut in 2019 at the Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles before touring the country.

Brathwaite was born in 1938 to Barbadian immigrants, in what he referred to as “the People’s Republic of Brooklyn” in Newly introduced York, though his family moved from there to Harlem and then to the South Bronx when Brathwaite was 5 years old. He attended the School of Industrial Art (now the High School of Art and Design) and, according to profiles of Brathwaite in T Magazine and Vice, was drawn to photography by two moments. The first was in August of 1955, when a 17-year-old Brathwaite encountered David Jackson’s haunting photograph of a brutalized Emmett Till in his open casket. The second was in 1956, when — after he and his brother Elombe co-founded the African Jazz Arts Society and Studios (AJASS) — Brathwaite saw a young man taking photos in a dark jazz club without the use of a flash, and his mind became alight with possibility.

Sources indicate that using a Hasselblad medium-format camera, Brathwaite attempted to do the same, learning to work with limited light in a manner that enhanced the visual narrative of his imagery. He would soon also develop a darkroom technique that enriched and deepened how Black skin would appear in his photography, honing the practice in a small darkroom in his Harlem apartment. Brathwaite went on to photograph jazz legends performing throughout the 1950s and ’60s, including Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Thelonious Monk and others.

“You want to get the feeling, the mood that you’re experiencing when they’re playing,” Brathwaite told Aperture Magazine in 2017. “That’s the thing. You want to capture that.”.

A 106-year-old from the Philippines is Vogue's oldest ever cover model.

It has been revealed that by the early 1960s, alongside the rest of AJASS, Brathwaite began using his photography and organizing prowess to consciously push back against whitewashed, Eurocentric beauty standards. The group came up with the concept of the Grandassa Models, young Black women whom Brathwaite would photograph, celebrating and accentuating their features. In 1962, AJASS organized “Naturally ’62”, a fashion show held in a Harlem club called the Purple Manor and featuring the models. The show would go on to be held regularly until 1992. In 1966, Brathwaite married his wife Sikolo, a Grandassa Model whom he had met on the street the year prior when he asked if he could take her portrait. The two remained married for the rest of Brathwaite’s life.

Industry observers note that by the 1970s, Brathwaite’s focus on jazz shifted to other forms of popular Black music. In 1974, he traveled to Africa with the Jackson Five to document their tour, also photographing the historic “Rumble in the Jungle” boxing match between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in what’s now the Democratic Republic of Congo that same year. Commissions in this era also saw Brathwaite photographing Nina Simone, Stevie Wonder, Sly and the Family Stone, Bob Marley and other music legends.

Creating for community: The Black designers placing identity and heritage at the center of their brands.

Throughout the ensuing decades, Brathwaite continued to explore and develop his mode of photography, all through the lens of the “Black is Beautiful” ethos. In 2016, Brathwaite joined the roster of Philip Martin Gallery in Los Angeles, and he was continuing to photograph commissions as recently as 2018, when he shot artist and stylist Joanne Petit-Frère for The Upcoming Yorker.

According to recent reports, T Magazine’s 2021 profile, published on the occasion of Brathwaite’s retrospective traveling to the Blanton Museum of Art in Austin, Texas, noted that the photographer’s health was failing such that he was unable to be interviewed for the article. A separate exhibition, “Kwame Brathwaite: Things Well Worth Waiting For,” is presently on view at the Art Institute of Chicago, where it will remain until July 24.

Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.
  • For Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic.
  • Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.

For Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic. That relationship looks more complicated from Beijing and Moscow.

Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran. But both have broader interests in their relationships with the United States and may see Iran partly through the prism of their own negotiations with Washington.

That raises a central question: Can Trump's strategy of economically isolating Iran succeed if China and Russia refuse to fully cooperate?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

China is currently the most important destination for Iranian oil.

In 2025, it was reported that Chinese buyers took more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports, much of it through independent refiners and at a steep discount because of sanctions.

As China provided Tehran an economic lifeline, Iran also became increasingly dependent on Chinese manufactured goods, machinery and industrial inputs.

Mohsen Solhdoost, an assistant professor of international relations at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, says China is notable to Washington's strategy but not decisive on its own.

"If the objective is to reduce Iranian export earnings, restrict access to equipment and make economic and military recovery more difficult, the United States can achieve substantial results without Chinese cooperation," he told DW.

But forcing Iran to accept Washington's preferred nuclear or regional policies is another matter.

"The ability to interrupt trade is much easier to demonstrate than the ability to determine another government's political choices," Solhdoost noted.

That distinction has become more crucial as US sanctions enforcement and maritime blockade efforts have increased pressure on Iranian crude oil exports.

In November, Washington announced Task Force Iron Gate, an initiative aimed at disrupting the movement of sanctioned goods, military equipment and revenue through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Even so, these trade links have not disappeared. The commercial and security interests of countries including Iraq, Pakistan and Turkey mean that goods continue to move across the region, albeit under greater scrutiny.

As a result, China's role in Iran's economy remains significant, but Solhdoost argues that demand alone cannot sustain Iranian exports. The oil must be able to reach international markets.

"A Chinese buyer cannot keep Iranian export revenues flowing simply by remaining willing to buy if newly loaded tankers cannot reach the market," Solhdoost noted.

This economic pressure is shaping Tehran's financial planning. A senior official at Iran's Proposal and Budget Organization recently mentioned the government was preparing its 2027-2028 budget under several scenarios, including one in which oil revenue falls to zero.

In a recent development, that does not mean Iran has adopted a zero-oil budget, but considering such a scenario illustrates how seriously Tehran views the situation. At the same time, Chinese trade can preserve critical parts of the Iranian economy even if overall commerce shrinks.

It has been revealed that machinery, electronics, spare parts and industrial components can still reach Iran by rail and road. Such trade cannot replace maritime commerce at comparable scale or cost, but it can keep selected factories and infrastructure operating.

Such Chinese support could help Iran endure pressure without preventing economic deterioration, claims Solhdoost.

But even for Beijing, supporting Iran economically does not mean supporting every Iranian policy.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has maintained support for cooperation with Tehran while calling for negotiations, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and stable energy supplies.

A prolonged conflict around Hormuz threatens wider energy supplies and global shipping. China therefore benefits from continued access to Iranian oil but also from regional stability.

Sources indicate that russia creates another obstacle to Iran's isolation. The two countries share access to the Caspian Sea and have expanded military, transport and economic cooperation.

Recent findings suggest that iranian officials have discussed ways of using Russian and northern trade routes to reduce the impact of American restrictions. There has also been speculation about oil swaps and deeper Russian assistance, although these claims remain difficult to verify.

Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, believes the summit should be viewed within a larger attempt to manage the wars in both Ukraine and the Middle East.

"Russia, China and the United States appear to be seeking constructive dialogue and results that could shape a newly introduced security architecture in the international system," Vakhshiteh told DW.

Solhdoost also warns against overstating Russian support for Iran.

The strategic partnership between Moscow and Tehran provides for security cooperation and efforts to counter unilateral sanctions, but it does not require Russia to enter a war on Iran's behalf.

Since Russia is deeply engaged in Ukraine, it likely has its own priorities in negotiations with Washington, claims Solhdoost.

"Russia would prioritize its own national interests in negotiations with the US over Ukraine and Iran," he said.

Moscow could support Iran while simultaneously using its relationship with Tehran as leverage in talks with Trump over Ukraine.

Sources indicate that for Iran, ties with China and Russia remain essential. They provide alternative trade routes, export markets and diplomatic support that complicate Washington's efforts to isolate Tehran.

Yet neither Beijing nor Moscow views Iran solely through the lens of strategic partnership. Both weigh support for Tehran against their own economic interests, security concerns and dealings with Washington.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Signal blocking screenshots to keep AI assistants out of private chats

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A screenshot is how a lot of things get saved on a phone, from a dinner reservation to the address a friend just texted.
  • According to recent reports, signal, a nonprofit messaging app that uses end-to-end encryption to keep texts and calls private, is putting limits on what those assistants can see.
  • On iPhones running iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting is on by default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A screenshot is how a lot of things get saved on a phone, from a dinner reservation to the address a friend just texted. AI assistants like Meta's Muse and Apple's Siri AI can now use what’s on the screen to answer questions or do things like add events to a calendar.

But not every platform is okay with that.

According to recent reports, signal, a nonprofit messaging app that uses end-to-end encryption to keep texts and calls private, is putting limits on what those assistants can see. On Friday, Nov. 20, the app unveiled it will block screenshots on iPhones running iOS 27 and restrict AI screen capture on some Android devices.

On iPhones running iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting is on by default. On supported Android devices, Signal automatically turns on Screen security when it detects an assistant trying to read what's on the screen. People can turn either protection off in Signal's settings, though doing so could give an assistant with screen access a look at both sides of the conversation.

Recent findings suggest that "Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it," wrote Signal President Meredith Whittaker in Signal's blog post. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

End-to-end encryption keeps a message private on its way from one person to another. When it arrives, the recipient's phone has to turn it back into words they can read. Those words might show up in the chat itself or in a notification.

Industry observers note that an AI assistant with access to either can read those messages, too. Once it has the text, Signal has no say in whether the assistant processes it on the phone or sends it to a remote server, according to their blog post.

That can play out in surprisingly ordinary ways. Earlier this week, Reuters reported that a Meta employee got a reminder from the firm’s Muse assistant to reply to her sister. The message was in Signal. "This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this," the employee wrote in an internal post.

Reuters worked with Signal and the AI Now Institute to see how that could happen using an Android phone and a Mac. They discovered that on the phone, Muse got the message text straight from a notification. On a Mac, it used accessibility tools and screenshots to read chats. In both tests, Muse relied on permissions granted during setup. Meta told Reuters that Muse can only access other apps through permissions customers explicitly grant.

According to recent reports, whittaker pointed to accessibility tools, which are designed to help people with disabilities use their devices. With broad permissions, she wrote, those tools can act as "a skeleton key that provides access to AI agents.".

She's thereby asking Apple, Google, and Microsoft to spell out what their assistants can read and give developers a way to block that access.

Topics Cybersecurity Privacy Meta.
